# Strict convexity and differentiability of the planar exponential first-passage limit shape

```json
{
  "abstract_verbatim": "We prove that the limit shape of undirected nearest-neighbor first-passage percolation on ℤ<sup>2</sup> with independent exponential edge weights is strictly convex and has a <i>C</i><sup>1</sup> boundary. This resolves the strict convexity and differentiability conjectures for the planar exponential model. More generally, we prove differentiability of the time-constant norm for every Gamma edge-weight law with positive shape and rate.",
```

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> We prove that the limit shape of undirected nearest-neighbor first-passage percolation on ℤ<sup>2</sup> with independent exponential edge weights is strictly convex and has a <i>C</i><sup>1</sup> boundary. This resolves the strict convexity and differentiability conjectures for the planar exponential model. More generally, we prove differentiability of the time-constant norm for every Gamma edge-weight law with positive shape and rate.

- **claim-exponential-shape** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-exponential-shape)): For independent exponential edge weights of any rate $\lambda>0$, the norm $\mu$ is Fréchet differentiable on $\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\}$, and its unit ball is strictly convex. In particular, $$\mu((1-t)x+ty)<1 \quad\text{if }x,y\in\partial\mathcal B,\ x\ne y,\ 0<t<1,$$ and $\partial\mathcal B$ is a $C^1$ curve with a unique supporting line at every point.
  - Explanation: For the planar exponential model, the deterministic norm has no corners away from the origin and its unit ball has no nontrivial supporting faces. The boundary has a unique supporting line at each point.
- **claim-gamma-differentiability** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-gamma-differentiability)): For independent Gamma edge weights with any fixed shape $\kappa>0$ and rate $\lambda>0$, the norm $\mu$ is Fréchet differentiable at every nonzero vector, and $\partial\mathcal B$ is a $C^1$ curve.
  - Explanation: Every fixed positive-shape, positive-rate Gamma law gives a differentiable time-constant norm away from the origin and a continuously differentiable boundary. Strict convexity for the whole Gamma family is not asserted.
- **claim-gamma-moments** (bound, [source](#stmt-df-ga-moment)): For $\tau\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(\kappa,\lambda)$ and $\theta<\lambda$, $$\mathbb Ee^{\theta\tau} =\left(\frac{\lambda}{\lambda-\theta}\right)^\kappa.$$ If $V$ is the sum over a deterministic set of $M$ distinct edges and $M\le A v$, where $A,v>0$, then $$\label{df:eq:gamma-sum-tail} \mathbb P\left(V>\frac{2A\kappa}{\lambda}v\right) \le \exp\{-A\kappa(1-\log 2)v\}.$$
  - Explanation: Integrating the Gamma density gives its exponential moment. Independence and exponential Markov inequality then bound the upper tail of a sum over distinct deterministic edges.
- **claim-extreme-support-contact** (theorem, [source](#stmt-df-prelim-supports)): The linear functionals $f_-$, $f_+$, and $f$ are bounded above by $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^2$ and equal $\mu$ at $u$. For $\sigma\in\{-,+\}$, with the corresponding numerical sign when multiplied by a scalar, $$\label{df:eq:support-contact} \mu(u+te_2)-f_\sigma(u+te_2)=o(\|t\|) \qquad(t\to0,\ \sigma t>0).$$
  - Explanation: The extreme transverse derivatives and their average define global supports of the norm. Each extreme support has first-order contact on its corresponding side.
- **claim-localized-travel** (theorem, [source](#stmt-df-cr-local-travel)): Fix $D,\eta,\delta>0$. Uniformly over deterministic vertices $p,q\in\mathbb Z^2$ with $\|q-p\|\le Ds$, the probability tends to one as $s\to\infty$ that there is a path from $p$ to $q$ with cost at most $$\mu(q-p)+\eta s$$ whose vertices are within distance $\delta s$ of the segment $[p,q]$.
  - Explanation: Uniformly over deterministic nearby endpoints, a path with small additive norm error can be confined near their joining segment with probability tending to one.
- **claim-interval-travel** (theorem, [source](#stmt-df-cr-interval-travel)): Fix $D,\eta,\delta>0$. Let $I_1,I_2$ be deterministic vertical intervals on lattice columns, and suppose that the diameter of $I_1\cup I_2$ is at most $Ds$. Uniformly over their locations, with probability tending to one as $s\to\infty$, every pair $p\in I_1\cap\mathbb Z^2$, $q\in I_2\cap\mathbb Z^2$ can be joined by a path of cost at most $\mu(q-p)+\eta s$ within distance $\delta s$ of $[p,q]$.
  - Explanation: Deterministic nets and vertical attachments put all endpoint pairs from the prescribed intervals on a common high-probability connection event. Endpoints may then be selected from the observed environment.
- **claim-high-density-oriented-path** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-df-cr-oriented-paths)): For every integer $k_0\ge0$ there is $\zeta=\zeta(k_0)>0$ with the following property. Let $(G_v)_{v\in\mathbb Z^2}$ be events such that any finite family indexed by sites at pairwise sup distance greater than $k_0$ is independent. If $\mathbb P(G_v^c)\le\zeta$ for every $v$, then with positive probability there is an infinite path starting at $0$, using steps $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$, all of whose sites satisfy $G_v$.
  - Explanation: A sufficiently small uniform failure probability produces an infinite good oriented path with positive probability when separated site tests are jointly independent. Stationarity is unnecessary.
- **claim-rare-fast-crossings** (bound, [source](#stmt-df-cr-rare-fast)): Fix $A,R,\varepsilon>0$ and $\sigma\in\{-,+\}$. As $s\to\infty$ and $n/s\to\infty$, with $s$ real and $n$ a positive integer, $$\label{df:eq:cr-rare-fast} \mathbb P\left( \begin{array}{l} \text{there is a path $P$ from $x=0$ to $x=n$ with} \ H_\sigma(P)<-\varepsilon s,\\ \text{all of whose vertices satisfy } -An\le x\le(1+A)n,\quad \|r\|\le Rs \end{array}\right)\longrightarrow0.$$ The same assertion holds, with the same probability, for every exact lattice translate of the event.
  - Explanation: Independent parallel trials amplify a hypothetical persistent crossing probability. One-sided support contact permits connectors whose cost preserves the deficit, contradicting the uniform shape theorem.
- **claim-cubic-crossing-rarity** (bound, [source](#stmt-df-gr-tilt)): For $s=2^k$ and $k\to\infty$, $$\mathbb P\bigl(E(s,s^3)\bigr)\longrightarrow0.$$
  - Explanation: Scaling the finitely many strip weights turns an allowed crossing into a fast crossing. The exact Gamma likelihood second moment remains bounded at cubic length and transfers rarity back to the original law.
- **claim-characteristic-lengths** (construction, [source](#stmt-df-gr-characteristic-lengths)): For every fixed $C>0$, $$\label{df:eq:gr-short-crossings} \mathbb P(E(s,n))\longrightarrow1 \qquad\text{as }s\to\infty,\quad 1\leq n\leq Cs,\quad n\in\mathbb N.$$ There is therefore an integer $k_0\geq0$ such that, for every $k\geq k_0$, the first dyadic integer $L_k\in\{1,2,4,\ldots\}$ satisfying $$\label{df:eq:gr-characteristic-threshold} \mathbb P(E(s_k,L_k))\leq q_0$$ exists. These lengths satisfy $$\label{df:eq:gr-characteristic-bounds} L_k\leq2^{3k},\qquad \frac{L_k}{2^k}\longrightarrow\infty.$$ Moreover, every dyadic integer $l<L_k$ satisfies $\mathbb P(E(s_k,l))>q_0$.
  - Explanation: Short crossings are likely, while cubic crossings are rare. The first dyadic probability threshold therefore defines characteristic lengths that grow faster than their widths without requiring monotonicity of crossing events.
- **claim-record-scales** (construction, [source](#stmt-df-gr-record-scales)): There is an infinite set $\mathcal K\subset\{k_0,k_0+1,\ldots\}$ such that, for $k\in\mathcal K$ and every integer $0\leq j\leq k-k_0$, $$\label{df:eq:gr-record-comparison} L_{k-j}\geq2^{-4j}L_k.$$
  - Explanation: Strict record minima of the rescaled characteristic lengths give an infinite subsequence with geometric comparison to every earlier scale.
- **claim-simultaneous-grid-connections** (construction, [source](#stmt-df-gr-grid-tools)): There is a constant $C_1$, independent of $A,R,J,j,k$, and for each fixed $A,R$ a sequence $\beta_J\to0$, such that the following holds. For every fixed $J\ge1$ and all sufficiently large $k\in\mathcal K$, there is an event $G_{k,J}$ with $$\mathbb P(G_{k,J}^{\mathrm c})\le\beta_J$$ on which the following connections exist simultaneously. For every level $J\le j\le j_*$, every grid interval $$[X,X+l_j]\subset[-(A+4)L,(A+4)L],\qquad X\in l_j\mathbb Z,$$ every real $r_0$ with $\left\lvert r_0\right\rvert\le Rs$, and every pair of lattice vertices $p,q$ on its left and right endpoint columns with $$\left\lvert r(p)-r_0\right\rvert\le1,\qquad\left\lvert r(q)-r_0\right\rvert\le1,$$ there is a path from $p$ to $q$ whose cost is at most $$\label{df:eq:gr-grid-cost} m_0l_j+C_1j^2w_j,$$ and whose vertices satisfy $$\label{df:eq:gr-grid-localization} X-l_j\le x\le X+2l_j,\qquad \left\lvert r-r_0\right\rvert\le C_1j^2w_j.$$ One may take $C_1=K+200\kappa/\lambda$. Thus $C_1$ may depend on $K,\kappa,\lambda$; the sequence $\beta_J$ may depend on $A,R,q_0,\kappa,\lambda$.
  - Explanation: Separated crossing trials and whole-interval attachment tests give simultaneous connections across every used mesh level, column interval, transverse target, and endpoint pair. Their error probabilities have a summable tail.
- **claim-arbitrary-endpoint-rarity** (bound, [source](#stmt-df-gr-variable-endpoints)): For every fixed $A,R,\varepsilon>0$, $$\label{df:eq:gr-variable-endpoints} \mathbb P\left( \begin{array}{c} \text{there is a finite path }P\text{ in } \{\left\lvert x\right\rvert\leq AL,\ \left\lvert r\right\rvert\leq Rs\}\\ \text{with }H_+(P)<-\varepsilon s\text{ or }H_-(P)<-\varepsilon s \end{array}\right)\longrightarrow0$$ as $k\to\infty$ through $\mathcal K$. The endpoints of $P$ may be any vertices of the region. The convergence is uniform over lattice translations of the region.
  - Explanation: Nested grid attachments move arbitrary observed endpoints to finitely many coarse columns at small total defect cost. Rare-fast crossing bounds then exclude substantial negative defects uniformly over translations.
- **claim-continuous-path-bk** (bound, [source](#stmt-df-wi-continuous-bk)): Let $A_1,\ldots,A_q$ be a finite list of events. For each $j$, suppose $A_j$ is the existence of a path $P$ in a prescribed family of finite lattice paths, all of whose edges belong to a fixed finite edge set, satisfying $$\tau(P)<b_j(P),$$ where $b_j(P)$ is deterministic. A family may include several labeled copies of a path with different bounds. Let $D(A_1,\ldots,A_q)$ be the event that one can choose a witnessing path for each event with pairwise disjoint edge sets. Then $$\label{df:wi:bk-bound} \mathbb P(D(A_1,\ldots,A_q))\le\prod_{j=1}^q\mathbb P(A_j).$$ The events in the list need not be distinct.
  - Explanation: Monotone quantile rounding reduces strict path witnesses to finite independent bit certificates. Edge-disjoint witnesses give the product probability bound even when event labels repeat.
- **claim-cheap-chunk-witness** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-df-wi-chunk-witness)): If a full chunk $Q$ with index $(i,h)$ satisfies $H(Q)<\eta s$, then its edges contain a path witness for $\mathcal A_{i,h}$.
  - Explanation: A cheap full chunk either exits transversely and pays the support gap, or contains a cheap forward crossing after its outer pieces are checked. A backward exit is incompatible with the defect bound.
- **claim-chunk-defect-multiplicity** (bound, [source](#stmt-df-wi-chunk-defect)): Every chunk, including the remainder, satisfies $$\label{df:wi:basic-defect} H(Q)\ge-\eta s-2\eta s M_Q.$$ A full chunk satisfies the stronger bound $$\label{df:wi:full-defect} H(Q)\ge\eta s-4\eta s M_Q.$$ If $M_{\rm tot}$ denotes the sum of $M_Q$ over the $N$ full chunks and the remainder of $P$, then $$\label{df:wi:total-defect} H(P)\ge(N-1)\eta s-4\eta s M_{\rm tot}.$$ The path contains $M_{\rm tot}$ pairwise edge-disjoint witnesses, assigned to the corresponding chunk indices, even if some indices repeat.
  - Explanation: Stopping at successive negative-defect prefixes bounds chunk deficit by its maximum witness multiplicity. Summing over a simple path preserves edge-disjointness even when coarse indices repeat.
- **claim-uniform-long-path-defect** (bound, [source](#stmt-df-wi-long-paths)): At the fixed scale chosen above, almost surely there exists a finite $N_0$ such that every finite simple path $P$ starting at the origin and having $N\ge N_0$ full chunks satisfies $$\label{df:wi:long-path-bound} H(P)\ge\frac12 N\eta s.$$
  - Explanation: Coarse itinerary and witness-allocation counts combine with BK to make low-defect paths summably unlikely. The eventual positive defect bound holds simultaneously for all sufficiently long simple paths from the origin.
- **claim-no-corner** (theorem, [source](#stmt-df-wi-no-corner)): For every $b\in[-1,1]$, the two one-sided transverse derivatives at $u=(1,b)$ agree: $$a_-=a_+.$$
  - Explanation: A positive transverse slope gap would impose linear defect on approximate minimizers along the contact direction, while the shape theorem makes that defect sublinear. The deterministic norm therefore has equal one-sided slopes.
- **claim-convex-boundary-equivalence** (classification, [source](#stmt-df-convex-regularity)): For a norm on $\mathbb R^2$, Fréchet differentiability at every nonzero vector is equivalent to uniqueness of the supporting line at every point of its unit sphere. These conditions are also equivalent to the unit sphere being a regular $C^1$ curve.
  - Explanation: For a planar norm, differentiability away from the origin, uniqueness of supporting lines, and regular continuous differentiability of the unit sphere are equivalent. This does not itself imply strict convexity.
- **claim-uniform-metric-errors** (bound, [source](#stmt-model-metric)): There are constants $C,c>0$ such that, for $x,y\in\mathbb Z^2$ and $R=\|x-y\|_1\ge2$, $$\begin{aligned} 0\le \mathbb ET(x,y)-\mu(y-x) &\le C\sqrt{R\log(2+R)},\label{model:mean}\\ \mathbb P\bigl(\|T(x,y)-\mathbb ET(x,y)\|\ge t\sqrt R\bigr) &\le C e^{-ct},\qquad t\ge0.\label{model:concentration} \end{aligned}$$ Consequently, for any fixed $p,C_0<\infty$ and $\alpha\in(1/2,1)$, with probability tending to one all pairs in $[-n^p,n^p]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$ at distance at most $C_0n$ satisfy $$\|T(x,y)-\mu(y-x)\|\le n^\alpha.$$ The expected maximum lower deficit over those pairs is at most $C_{p,C_0}\sqrt n\log(2+n)$. The same conclusions hold for metric-graph endpoints after adding an $O(\log n)$ term in expectation.
  - Explanation: Mean approximation and exponential concentration control polynomially many endpoint pairs simultaneously. Integrated lower deficits and incident-edge corrections extend the estimates to metric-graph endpoints.
- **claim-random-cut-period-identity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-fb-random-cuts)): For any admissible $d$-road, $$\mathbb E[P_n(X_{i+1})-P_n(X_i)]=0, \qquad \mathbb ED_n(\gamma[i,i+1]) =\mathbb EQ_n(\gamma[i,i+1])\ge0. \label{eq:fb-period-identity}$$ Here $\gamma[i,i+1]$ denotes the oriented road portion between its marked cuts.
  - Explanation: Covariant marked cuts have equal expected centered calibration values. Hence expected road defect equals expected raw excess, even though the centered calibration at an individual random cut need not have mean zero.
- **claim-no-long-cheap-paths** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-fb-cheap-paths)): Let $V$ be a finite set of vertices of $\mathbb Z^2$. For every integer $R\ge1$ and $t\ge0$, $$\mathbb P\left( \begin{array}{c} \text{some self-avoiding path starting in $V$ has}\\[-2pt] \text{at least $R$ edges and cost at most $t$} \end{array}\right) \le \frac83 \|V\|e^{5t}2^{-R}. \label{eq:fb-cheap-bound}$$ Consequently there are numerical constants $c,C>0$ such that, for $z\ne0$ and $R\ge40\|z\|_1$, the probability that a geodesic from $0$ to $z$ has at least $R$ edges is at most $Ce^{-cR}$.
  - Explanation: Counting self-avoiding paths and using a negative exponential moment bounds long cheap crossings. A coordinate-path comparison gives an exponential tail for geodesic edge count and ensures finite minimizers.
- **claim-road-sublinear-initialization** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-fb-upper)): For fixed $s,v,w$ there are admissible pairs of roads with $$b(n)\le C_s\sqrt n\log(2+n)\le C'_s n^{3/4} \label{eq:fb-upper}$$ for all sufficiently large multiples of a fixed integer. The constants may depend on $s$; the exponent $3/4$ does not.
  - Explanation: Concatenating geodesics restricted to small balls gives local admissible roads. Metric errors and rare escape events yield a sublinear common period bound.
- **claim-road-positive-infimum** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-fb-positive)): There is $c_0>0$, depending only on the fixed flat and the dependence radius $10$, such that $$b(n)\ge c_0 \label{eq:fb-positive}$$ for all sufficiently large admissible $n$. The constant $c_0$ is independent of the road rules, of sufficiently small $s$, and of the nearby rational directions. The lower threshold on $n$ may depend on $s$ and the divisibility requirements.
  - Explanation: A local weight decrease creates a competing-route saving while leaving the other route and its endpoints fixed. Total-variation transfer forces a positive period-defect lower bound uniform over road rules.
- **claim-local-increment-network** (construction, [source](#stmt-found-lem-network)): Let $A=v+sw$, $B=w+sv$ with $0<s<1/4$, and suppose two road rules have tracking radius $r$ and dependence radius $10$ in $\\|\cdot\\|_*$, and expected defect at most $\beta$ on each marked unit period. There exist numerical constants $r_0,H,C>0$ with the following property whenever $r<r_0$ and $n\geq K_{\rm lat}/r$.* *One can choose a random anchor $X_z$ near each point $z_1A+z_2B$, $z\in\mathbb Z^2$, and, for $i=1,2$, a random variable $E_{z,i}$ such that $$\mathbb E\left\|E_{z,i}-P(X_{z+e_i})+P(X_z)\right\| \leq C\beta. \label{found:eq-increment}$$ The variable $E_{z,i}$ uses only input cells at index distance at most $H$ from $z$. Here an input cell contains all microscopic weights and private inputs assigned to the corresponding unit parallelogram.* *One may also prescribe any collection of additional marked anchors $X_{z,\lambda}$, each on a translated $A$- or $B$-road within a fixed distance of $z_1A+z_2B$. There are comparisons of the same kind between any two such anchors at the same or neighboring indices. Their constants depend on that distance, but not on the number of labels $\lambda$.
  - Explanation: Planar intersections of the road families produce a comparison grid. Bounded signed trips estimate calibration increments with errors controlled by complete-period defects, including additional anchor labels.
- **claim-finite-cell-local-potential** (construction, [source](#stmt-found-lem-finite-cell)): Let $(\eta_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^2}$ be independent random elements and let $V_{z,\lambda}\in L^1$, where $\lambda$ belongs to an arbitrary label set with a distinguished label $0$. Set $\mathcal F_I=\sigma(\eta_z:z\in I)$ and $Q_H(z)=z+[-H,H]^2\cap\mathbb Z^2$, with integer $H\geq2$. Suppose that whenever $\|z-z'\|_1\leq1$, and for every pair of labels in question, there is an $\mathcal F_{Q_H(z)}$-measurable variable $E_{(z,\lambda),(z',\lambda')}$ such that $$\left\\|E_{(z,\lambda),(z',\lambda')} -V_{z',\lambda'}+V_{z,\lambda}\right\\|_1 \leq\varepsilon. \label{found:eq-abstract-hyp}$$ Then there are random variables $g_{z,\lambda}$, measurable with respect to $\mathcal F_{Q_{R+2H}(z)}$, where $R=8H+20$, such that $$\begin{aligned} \mathbb Eg_{z,\lambda}&=\mathbb EV_{z,\lambda},\label{found:eq-mean}\\ \left\\|g_{z',\lambda'}-g_{z,\lambda} -V_{z',\lambda'}+V_{z,\lambda}\right\\|_1 &\leq C_H\varepsilon. \label{found:eq-potential} \end{aligned}$$ The constant $C_H$ depends only on $H$, not on the number of labels. Translation covariance is preserved whenever the true increment field $V_{z',\lambda'}-V_{z,\lambda}$ is covariant under measure-preserving input shifts and the deterministic means have the required covariance.
  - Explanation: Finite inclusion–exclusion projections integrate approximate local increments into local potentials. An exterior detour bounds cutoff errors, preserving means and translation covariance without dependence on the number of labels.
- **claim-uniform-local-envelopes** (bound, [source](#stmt-found-lem-envelope)): Fix $m$ road labels and parameter windows of length at most $L$ contained in a bounded macroscopic neighborhood of a deterministic cell. There is a nonnegative local random variable $U$ with $\mathbb EU\leq C_{m,L}\beta$ which bounds all of the following: absolute corrected signed costs within these windows; sums with a bounded number of switches between these labels at intersections; and the gauge differences for such switches at their common physical vertex. The support radius depends only on $L$, the neighborhood size, and the original road locality radius.* *If a physical path is confined to a prescribed deterministic finite closed metric subgraph and has endpoints on two of the windows, its corrected cost, including signed adjustments to prescribed center anchors, is bounded below by $-U'$ for a local nonnegative variable $U'$ with $\mathbb EU'\leq C_{m,L}\beta$. Its support also includes the prescribed subgraph. This bound holds simultaneously for every such path and every choice of its endpoints.
  - Explanation: Local extrema of corrected costs provide envelopes for all attachment occurrences and switches. Calibration domination controls physical competitors from below without requiring local pointwise bounds for absolute calibration errors.
- **claim-linear-scale-gauge-tails** (bound, [source](#stmt-found-lem-gauge-tail)): Suppose the period excess bound satisfies $\beta\leq C_s n^\alpha$ for some fixed $\alpha<1$. Fix the neighborhood and finitely many labels of Lemma <a href="#found:lem-envelope" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="found:lem-envelope">29</a>. After subtraction of one common deterministic reference-label mean, a local random variable $V$ bounds the absolute gauges at all those occurrences and the absolute raw signed $Q$-costs of their bounded road adjustments. For any fixed $\alpha'\in(\max\{\alpha,1/2\},1)$, Lemma <a href="#model:metric" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="model:metric">20</a> gives $$\mathbb EV\leq C_s n^{\alpha'},\qquad \mathbb P(V>\epsilon n)\leq C_s\epsilon^{-1}n^{\alpha'-1}.$$ The constants may depend on the fixed neighborhood and label collection.
  - Explanation: A sublinear period bound and metric deficit estimates control absolute local gauges and raw adjustment costs after common deterministic centering. Markov inequality gives a vanishing linear-scale tail.
- **claim-common-incoming-gauge** (construction, [source](#stmt-found-lem-common-gauge)): Fix deterministic tubes and a baseline road contained in one of them. Write $\eta=(\eta_0,\eta_{\rm other})$ for all preserved tube weights, where $\eta_0$ consists exactly of the weights in the baseline’s own tube and $\eta_{\rm other}$ contains the remaining preserved edges. Let $\xi$ contain the baseline’s private road seeds and a private completion of the entire complement of its own tube. Construct the baseline once, using the actual weights in its own tube and these private inputs everywhere else. The resulting road is a function of $(\eta_0,\xi)$ alone.* *In each world $j$, retain all prescribed tube weights and use an iid completion $\zeta^j$ elsewhere. For every $j$, the private input $\xi$ is independent of the joint tuple $(\eta,\zeta^j)$; different worlds may share coordinates with one another. Assume that every world has the correct product weight law, uses the same measurable calibration map, and supplies the local comparison network above with period bound $\beta$. Assume also that the shared baseline is admissible in every world and has expected defect at most $\beta$ on each marked period there. The latter condition follows from the random-cut period identity when the shared baseline rule has period excess at most $\beta$.* *Let $g_x^j$ be the gauge given by <a href="#found:eq-gauge-formula" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="found:eq-gauge-formula">[found:eq-gauge-formula]</a> at a marked baseline anchor. There is a local function $g_x^{\rm in}$ of $(\eta_0,\xi)$ alone such that, in every world, $$\mathbb E\|g_x^j-g_x^{\rm in}\|\leq C\beta. \label{found:eq-common-gauge}$$ Its support radius and the constant $C$ are uniform in the number of worlds. After interpolation along any bounded baseline interval, the same assertion holds with an expected supremum bound of order $\beta$. No identification of the calibrations in different worlds is asserted. In particular, incoming gauges for disjoint baseline tubes with independent private completions and seeds are independent.
  - Explanation: Projected costs along the shared baseline define a local incoming gauge common to every exterior completion. Uniform comparison concerns gauge errors, not equality of the generally different calibrations.
- **claim-phase-locality-covariance** (theorem, [source](#stmt-phases-locality)): The averaged gauges retain the local bounds, means, interpolation identities, and common-tube comparisons of the preceding section. Their support radii and bounds do not acquire a factor $\|\mathcal H\|$. They are covariant under translation by $A$, and their laws are covariant under every row shift in $\mathcal H$.* *For a link or gauge in a fixed neighborhood of wall $j$, all random phase dependence is confined to a fixed number of wall indices near $j$. Together with the independent spatial inputs, this gives independence of entire columns at sufficiently separated indices. The separation constant is independent of $\|\mathcal H\|$ and $\sigma$.
  - Explanation: Averaging over deterministic mesh offsets preserves means, interpolation, and local comparison bounds. Local wall-phase dependence and disjoint spatial inputs give independence of sufficiently separated entire columns.
- **claim-sparse-path-indicators** (bound, [source](#stmt-probability-sparse)): Let $(I_z)_{z\in\mathbb Z^2}$ be indicators with $\mathbb P(I_z=1)\le p$. Suppose $\mathbb Z^2$ has a partition into $q$ classes such that the variables within each class are mutually independent. For every integer $L\ge0$, $$\mathbb E\max_{\pi\in\mathcal P_L}\sum_{z\in\pi}I_z \le C_q\min\{L+1,(L+1)\sqrt p,(L+1)^2p\}. \label{probability:sparse-bound}$$ The same conclusion, with adjusted constants, holds for lists of distinct sites whose initial distance from the origin plus the sum of their successive distances is at most $c(L+1)$, for fixed $c$. It also holds on any fixed full-rank planar lattice. In particular, it applies to a field with a fixed range of dependence.
  - Explanation: Counting lists of distinct marked sites under a travel budget yields sparse-path expectation bounds. Partitioning into independence classes extends the estimate to fixed dependence ranges and fixed planar lattices.
- **claim-integrated-selected-tails** (bound, [source](#stmt-probability-integrated-tails)): Let $(U_z)$ be nonnegative fields whose dependence range is uniform in a possible law index $n$, and suppose $\sup_{n,z}\mathbb P(U_z>t)\le p(t)$. Then, for $T\ge0$, $$\begin{aligned} \mathbb E\sup_{\pi\in\mathcal P_L} \sum_{z\in\pi}U_z\mathbf1_{\{U_z>T\}} &\le C(L+1)\left[T\sqrt{p(T)}+ \int_T^\infty\sqrt{p(t)}\,dt\right]. \label{probability:tail-integral} \end{aligned}$$ In particular, a uniform bound $\mathbb P(U_z>t)\le A t^{-4}$ for $t\ge1$ gives $C_A(L+1)/T$ for $T\ge1$. The same bounds hold for the site lists and bounded multiplicities in Lemma <a href="#probability:sparse" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="probability:sparse">34</a>.
  - Explanation: Layer-cake integration of sparse indicator bounds controls selected tail sums. The conclusion may be infinite when the square-root tail integral diverges; sufficiently light polynomial tails give a finite decaying bound.
- **claim-separated-candidate-selection** (construction, [source](#stmt-probability-candidates)): A fixed bounded region contains at most $J$ candidate cells. For each cell $c$, let $U_c\ge0$ be measurable with respect to a specified subset of one family of independent inputs, with $\mathbb EU_c\le A$. Suppose each admissible object provides a tuple of $m$ cells whose input supports are pairwise disjoint. There is a local random variable $V$ that bounds, simultaneously for every object, its smallest available $U_c$, and satisfies $$\mathbb P(V>t)\le J^m\min\{1,(A/t)^m\},\qquad t>0.$$ For fixed $J,m,A$, the fourth moment of $V$ is uniformly bounded when $m>4$. The same assertion holds conditional on auxiliary data if the disjoint supports retain their product law and each conditional first moment is at most the same deterministic $A$.
  - Explanation: Maximizing the minimum cost over every admissible separated candidate tuple gives a local bound valid before an object is selected. Product tails supply the stated moment control under unconditional or uniform conditional product laws.
- **claim-area-preserving-lattice-matching** (construction, [source](#stmt-probability-matching)): Let $\Lambda$ be a full-rank lattice in $\mathbb R^2$ and let $T$ be invertible with $\|\det T\|=1$. There is a bijection $\psi:\Lambda\to\Lambda$ and a finite $b_T$ such that $$\|\psi(z)-Tz\|\le b_T\qquad(z\in\Lambda).$$ For a bounded fundamental tile $Q$ of $\Lambda$, one may take $b_T\le\sup_{q,q'\in Q}\|Tq-q'\|$. For an affine map $Tz+a$, the same bound holds with $\|\psi(z)-(Tz+a)\|$ on the left.
  - Explanation: Equal-area tile intersections satisfy finite Hall conditions. Compactness produces a bijection of the infinite lattice with bounded error relative to the prescribed area-preserving linear or affine map.
- **claim-thin-diagram-geometry** (construction, [source](#stmt-probability-thin-geometry)): Fix $H,c>0$ and a full-rank lattice $\Lambda$. Suppose $z_1,\ldots,z_k\in\Lambda$ satisfy the all-pairs condition $$E^{-1}(z_j-z_i)\ge-H(1,1) \quad\hbox{coordinatewise for every }i<j, \label{probability:approximate-order}$$ and lie in the parallelogram $$E\big([-H,cN+H]\times[-H,\delta N+H]\big). \label{probability:thin-box}$$ For $F\ge1$, define $$T_F=\left(\frac{\det E}{\det U}\right)^{1/2} U\begin{pmatrix}F^{-1}&0\\0&F\end{pmatrix}E^{-1}.$$ Then $\det T_F=1$. A matching $\psi_F$ supplied by Lemma <a href="#probability:matching" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="probability:matching">37</a> sends these sites into a deterministic square of diameter at most $$C(N/F+F\delta N)+C_F. \label{probability:compressed-size}$$ For every fixed $r_0>0$, there is a finite $R_F$, uniform in $E$, such that, if $i<j$ and $\|z_j-z_i\|>R_F$, then $\psi_F(z_j)-\psi_F(z_i)\in\mathcal K$ and both coordinates of this increment exceed $r_0$.
  - Explanation: Reciprocal coordinate deformation compresses a thin diagram while preserving area. Bounded lattice-matching errors preserve forward cone order for sufficiently distant pairs under the all-pairs order hypothesis.
- **claim-weak-second-moment-tail** (bound, [source](#stmt-probability-weak-two)): Under <a href="#probability:collection-assumption" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="probability:collection-assumption">[probability:collection-assumption]</a>, $$\sup_n\mathbb P(Y_z>t)\le C\min\{1,t^{-2}\}, \qquad t>0.$$
  - Explanation: Testing the collection bound against a singleton maximum over independent sites yields a weak second-moment tail estimate. A finite second moment is not implied.
- **claim-negligible-thin-selected-tails** (bound, [source](#stmt-probability-thin-tails)): Assume <a href="#probability:collection-assumption" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="probability:collection-assumption">[probability:collection-assumption]</a>, and fix $H,c,m_0$. For $N\ge1$, let $\mathcal S(N,\delta)$ consist of finite site sequences satisfying <a href="#probability:approximate-order" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="probability:approximate-order">[probability:approximate-order]</a> and <a href="#probability:thin-box" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="probability:thin-box">[probability:thin-box]</a>, with at most $m_0$ occurrences per site. Suppose also that their distinct sites can be visited by a path whose initial distance from the origin plus total length is at most $c(N+1)$.* *For every $F\ge1$ there is $C_F<\infty$ such that, for $T\ge1$ and $0\le\delta\le F^{-2}$, $$\mathbb E\sup_{S\in\mathcal S(N,\delta)} \sum_{z\in S}Y_z\mathbf1_{\{Y_z>T\}} \le \frac{CN}{F}+\frac{C_F(N+1)}{T}+C_F. \label{probability:thin-tail-bound}$$ Here $C$ is independent of $F,T,\delta,n$. Consequently, for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are $\delta_0>0$ and $T_0<\infty$ such that, for every sequence of laws and every $N(n)\to\infty$, $$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac1{N(n)} \mathbb E\sup_{S\in\mathcal S(N(n),\delta_0)} \sum_{z\in S}Y_z\mathbf1_{\{Y_z>T_0\}} \le\varepsilon.$$ Finite sums of field types and independence sublattices satisfy the same conclusion if their number and all required constants are uniform.
  - Explanation: Nearby collisions have lighter tails, while separated retained values become a directed chain under a deterministic lattice permutation. Charging only that retained chain gives negligible selected tails after the ordered parameter choices.
- **claim-row-concentration-with-omissions** (bound, [source](#stmt-probability-rows)): For each $n$, let $W^{(n)}_{i,j}$, $i,j\in\mathbb Z$, be real random variables with $\|W^{(n)}_{i,j}\|\le B$. Suppose that for every deterministic sequence $(j_i)$, the variables $(W^{(n)}_{i,j_i})$ in each residue class $i\pmod q$ are mutually independent. The integer $q\ge1$ and $B<\infty$ are fixed. One sufficient condition is mutual independence of the sigma-fields generated by entire columns in any set of columns separated by at least $q$.* *Fix $d<\infty$ and $\varepsilon>0$. Consider rows with $\|j_1\|\le N^d$ and $\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}\|j_{i+1}-j_i\|\le\delta N$, and omission sets $O\subset\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $\|O\|\le\eta N$. For sufficiently small fixed $\delta,\eta>0$, depending only on $\varepsilon,B,q,d$, uniformly in $n$, $$\mathbb P\left( \sup_{(j_i),O}\left\| \sum_{i\notin O}\big(W^{(n)}_{i,j_i} -\mathbb EW^{(n)}_{i,j_i}\big) \right\|>\varepsilon N\right) \longrightarrow0\qquad(N\to\infty). \label{probability:row-concentration}$$ The convergence is exponential up to a polynomial factor. If all means equal $m_n$, the comparison sum is $m_n(N-\|O\|)$. The conclusion applies to indicators and to bounded sums over any fixed finite list of offsets or types that separately satisfy the hypotheses, with adjusted constants. A direct application to the sum requires independence at a spacing $q$ appropriate to its combined input supports.
  - Explanation: Hoeffding bounds on independent column residue classes defeat the entropy of low-variation rows and sparse omission sets. The supremum is taken before any environment-dependent selection.
- **claim-good-dyadic-levels** (construction, [source](#stmt-probability-dyadic)): Let $U_1^{(n)},\ldots,U_k^{(n)}$ be nonnegative variables with $$\sup_n\sum_{a=1}^k\mathbb EU_a^{(n)}\le A.$$ Fix $M_0>0$ and an integer $J\ge1$. For each $n$, there is $M_n\in\{M_0,2M_0,\ldots,2^{J-1}M_0\}$ such that $$M_n\sum_{a=1}^k\mathbb P(U_a^{(n)}>M_n) \le\frac{2A}{J}. \label{probability:good-level}$$ Thus this quantity can be made arbitrarily small within a fixed finite range of levels, uniformly over the laws. The level may depend on the law, but is deterministic for that law and is not chosen from the realization of the field.
  - Explanation: A finite geometric sum and averaging choose a deterministic level for each law with small threshold-weighted tail probability. This does not establish uniform integrability of discarded values.
- **claim-uniform-conditional-envelope** (construction, [source](#stmt-access-conditioning)): There is a local random variable $W_c$, with the same support as $U_c$, such that $$\label{access:all-conditionals} \mathbb E[U_c\mid\mathcal F_{\mathcal D}]\le W_c, \qquad \mathbb EW_c\le 2^{m_0}C\beta.$$ The inequalities hold simultaneously for every deterministic union-cell observation $\mathcal D$.
  - Explanation: Summing conditional expectations over every subset of the local input support gives a common envelope for all deterministic union-cell observations. Observation size does not enlarge the envelope's support.
- **claim-physical-center-cost-realization** (construction, [source](#stmt-access-physical)): There are exterior intersection occurrences $a$ on $W_-$ and $b$ on $W_+$, at bounded parameter distance from their cut windows, such that $a$ precedes every admissible $x,x_0$, $b$ follows every admissible $y,y_0$, and the input supports at $a,b$ lie beyond the corresponding observed $h$-faces. For every admissible internal path, the physical forward concatenation $a\to x$, $\pi$, $y\to b$ has corrected cost $$\label{access:physical-identity} H(\pi)+C_{W_-}(a,x_0)+C_{W_+}(y_0,b).$$ After including changes to exterior network labels, the absolute extra cost is bounded by $U_{c_-}+U_{c_+}$, enlarging the fixed local envelopes if necessary.
  - Explanation: Exterior intersections before and after the observed windows turn signed center-label bookkeeping into an actual forward path. The extra access and label-switch costs lie within fixed local envelopes.
- **claim-uniform-selected-cuts** (construction, [source](#stmt-access-selected-cuts)): Fix a polynomial-box exponent $q$ and an integer $m>4$. The integer $m$ can be increased so that $m\vartheta>q$. There are fixed radii $H_m$ and $K>20H_m$, a finite-range field $(E_z)$, and cuts of any continuous nearest-neighbor path at its successive $K$-exit marks, apart from bounded end portions, with the following properties.* 1. *Each selected cut is a road occurrence within $K/10$ of the corresponding exit mark. Consecutive selected cuts have displacement between $K/2$ and $2K$, and the intervening path piece has diameter $O(K)$.* 2. *If $c$ is its cut cell and $z$ the unit cell containing its exit mark, then $$\label{access:cut-control} W_c/\beta\le E_z,\qquad V_c\le a_n E_z.$$ All finitely many allowed labels and center conventions at that occurrence are included in these inequalities.* 3. *Uniformly in the input-road rule and $n$, $$\label{access:cut-tail} \mathbb P(E_z>t)\le C_K\min(1,t^{-m}),\qquad t>0.$$ In particular $\sup_{n,z}\mathbb EE_z^4<\infty$.* 4. *For any fixed $\varepsilon>0$, the probability that one of these cuts in a collection of at most $O(n^q)$ possible mark cells has $V_c>\varepsilon n$ tends to zero.* *The construction is valid simultaneously for all paths, including a path chosen after the entire environment has been observed. At an exit mark, call the portion after its last preceding hit of the boundary of its $H_m$-ball the terminal arc. Suppose a fine occurrence partition has segment traces of diameter at most $\delta_f$ in the present max norm, and every fine interval meeting that arc chronologically, including at an endpoint, has displacement in $$\label{access:horizontal-hyp} \mathcal G_\kappa=\{z:z_1\ge0,\ \|z_2\|\le\kappa z_1\}, \qquad 0\le\kappa<1, \qquad H_m>\frac{2(1+\kappa)}{1-\kappa}\delta_f.$$ Then all candidates for that mark may be taken on $B$-walls.
  - Explanation: Separated candidate tuples jointly minimize normalized access charge and raw gauge envelope. A maximum over all possible tuples makes the selection valid for paths inspected after the environment, with a lighter polynomial tail.
- **claim-tunnel-negative-cost-accounting** (bound, [source](#stmt-access-accounting)): If a path piece with the specified type has normalized center-label cost $c$, then $$\label{access:negative-accounting} c^-\le Y+W_{c_-}/\beta+W_{c_+}/\beta.$$ If $Y>0$, the internal minimizer has a physical forward realization between its exterior intersection labels whose conditional expected normalized corrected cost is at most $-Y$.
  - Explanation: The internal minimum bounds any observed piece's negative cost. Paying conditional forward-access charges leaves a tunnel reward whose positive values have a physical realization with negative conditional expected corrected cost.
- **claim-finite-volume-tunnel-collection** (bound, [source](#stmt-access-collection)): For the iid tunnel field associated with any fixed local type and phase template there are constants $C,C_0<\infty$, independent of $n$ and the input-road rule, such that the following holds. Let $G_n(L)$ be the maximum of $\sum_{p\in\Gamma}Y_p$ over finite distinct chains in an arbitrary deterministic translated coordinate square of side at most $L$, whose consecutive differences have both coordinates at least $2S$. The empty chain and singletons are allowed. Then $$\label{access:finite-volume} \mathbb EG_n(L)\le CL+C_0.$$ The same bound therefore holds if consecutive differences are additionally required to lie in any fixed inner cone of the positive quadrant.
  - Explanation: A maximizing observed tunnel chain can be joined by forward corridors whose entire input supports avoid every observation. Conditional access charges and calibration at fixed endpoint windows then bound expected collected reward linearly in its span.
- **claim-extreme-point-direction-modulus** (bound, [source](#stmt-links-extreme)): Let $a$ be an extreme point of the norm ball, let $S_\mu=\{z:\mu(z)=1\}$, and let $U$ be a relatively open neighborhood of $a$ in $S_\mu$. For $t\ge0$, put $$\omega_U(t)=\sup\left\{\nu(S_\mu\setminus U): \nu\in\mathcal P(S_\mu),\ \left\|\int z\,d\nu(z)-a\right\|\le t\right\}.$$ Then $\omega_U(t)\to0$ as $t\downarrow0$. If $N>0$, $0\le d_0<1/2$, and finitely many increments satisfy $$\left\|\sum_i z_i-Na\right\|\le d_0N,\qquad \left\|\sum_i\mu(z_i)-N\right\|\le d_0N,$$ then, with $C_a=2(1+\|a\|)$, $$\sum_{i:z_i/\mu(z_i)\notin U}\mu(z_i) \le (1+d_0)N\,\omega_U(C_a d_0). \label{links:extreme-modulus}$$ Zero increments are omitted. In particular, endpoint error $o(N)$ and total norm length $N+o(N)$ imply $o(N)$ norm mass outside $U$.
  - Explanation: Compactness and extremality force probability measures with barycenter near an extreme point to concentrate near that point. Applied to norm-weighted increments, this bounds the mass moving away from the chosen direction.
- **claim-density-halo-removal** (construction, [source](#stmt-links-halos)): Let $x_0,\ldots,x_m$ be successive cuts of a path. All distances in this lemma use the $(A,B)$ maximum norm. Suppose $K/2\le\|x_{i+1}-x_i\|\le CK$, and associate to each starting cut $x_i$ a center $z_i$ within a fixed distance $H_0$, independent of the cone enlargement. Declare an index bad when its increment is outside $\mathcal C_1$, or its physical subpath has a backward $h$-excursion of size at least one. Suppose, for $c_*>0$ and $\epsilon_n^{\rm raw}\to0$, its raw costs satisfy $$Q_i\ge-\epsilon_n^{\rm raw}n\quad\hbox{for all }i, \qquad Q_i\ge c_*n\quad\hbox{for bad }i.$$ Let effective cut labels satisfy $\|\widetilde g_i-g_{\rm ref}\|\le\lambda n$ for one common constant $g_{\rm ref}$. For sufficiently small $\lambda>0$ there is a set $R$ of removed indices containing all bad indices, of cardinality at most a fixed multiple of their number, for which* 1. *$\sum_{i\in R}(Q_i-\widetilde g_{i+1}+\widetilde g_i)\ge0$;* 2. *retained centers $z_i$ are in $\mathcal C_2$-order up to a bounded additive error, for every pair of retained indices;* 3. *the same order includes the initial and terminal points, up to a bounded additive error;* 4. *repetitions of any one center have bounded multiplicity, independently of how small the cone enlargement is.
  - Explanation: Removing intervals with excessive bad density enforces all-pairs cone order among retained centers. Positive raw penalties absorb removed endpoint-gauge differences, and forward progress bounds repeated-center multiplicity.
- **claim-uniform-geodesic-extraction** (construction, [source](#stmt-links-extraction)): For every sufficiently small fixed $\delta,\eta>0$, the final geometric choices above can be made so that there are deterministic $\epsilon_n,\pi_n\to0$ and fixed constants $H,C,C_K,c>0$ and integers $q_K,m_0$ with the following property. For each $\mathfrak r\in\mathfrak R_n$ there is an event $\Omega_{n,\mathfrak r}$ such that $$\sup_{\mathfrak r\in\mathfrak R_n} \mathbb P_{\mathfrak r}(\Omega_{n,\mathfrak r}^{\,c})\le\pi_n. \label{links:extraction-event}$$ Let $x_n^\star$ be a deterministic nearest vertex of $\mathcal G_n$ to $Na$, and put $$j_n=\left\lfloor u(x_n^\star)/d+\tfrac12\right\rfloor,\qquad \mathcal J_n=\{0,1,\ldots,j_n-1\}.$$ For large $n$, $cN\le j_n\le CN$. On $\Omega_{n,\mathfrak r}$, a geodesic from $0$ to $x_n^\star$ has consecutive selected pieces $\gamma_i:x_i\to x_{i+1}$, $0\le i<m_N$, after two bounded terminal fragments are removed, and the following objects and bounds.* 1. *There are at most $CN/K+C$ pieces, each of diameter $O(K)$, with consecutive cut displacement between $K/2$ and $2K$ in the $(A,B)$ maximum norm. The shared data in <a href="#links:piece-cost" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="links:piece-cost">[links:piece-cost]</a> have $\|\widetilde g_i-g_{\rm ref}\|\le\lambda n$. A removed set $R$ contains every bad piece of Lemma <a href="#links:halos" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="links:halos">49</a> and satisfies $$\|R\|\le\epsilon_nN,\qquad \sum_{i\in R}c_i^{\rm cost}\ge0,\qquad \sum_{i\notin R}c_i^{\rm cost}\le\epsilon_nN. \label{links:retained-cost}$$* 2. *The retained pieces have types $t_i$ from the fixed access family and centers $z_i$ on its fixed finite family of full-rank center lattices, after bounded rounding. Let $E=[e_1\ e_2]$, where the $e_j$ are the boundary generators of $\mathcal C_2$, normalized by $h(e_j)=1$ and ordered so that $e_1\to a$ and $e_2\to b$ as $\mathcal C_2$ shrinks to $\mathcal C$. In chronological order the centers satisfy $$E^{-1}(z_j-z_i)\ge-H(1,1)\quad(i<j),\qquad z_i\in E([-H,CN+H]\times[-H,\delta N+H]). \label{links:retained-geometry}$$ The inequality is coordinatewise. Each rounded site occurs at most $m_0$ times, and the initial distance from the origin plus total successive center distance is at most $C(N+1)$. These bounds persist on every type and sparse-residue subsequence. The matrices $E$ range in a fixed compact family, and $H,C,m_0$ remain bounded when the final cone is narrowed.* 3. *An irregular retained set $\mathcal I$ has $\|\mathcal I\|\le(C_K\eta+\epsilon_n)N$. Each $i\notin R\cup\mathcal I$ supplies at most $q_K$ admissible links $\mathcal L_i$, with $$c_i^{\rm cost}\ge\sum_{(j,k)\in\mathcal L_i}X_{j,k}/\beta. \label{links:unclipped-comparison}$$ In the chronological list $\mathcal L=\bigcup_{i\notin R\cup\mathcal I}\mathcal L_i$, columns are distinct, increasing, and belong to $\mathcal J_n$. For sufficiently small fixed $\eta$, $\|\mathcal L\|\ge cN$ for all large $n$, after decreasing $c$ once. If $k_1,\ldots,k_\ell$ are the selected rows, then $$\begin{gathered} \|\mathcal J_n\setminus\{j:(j,k)\in\mathcal L\}\| \le(C_K\eta+\epsilon_n)N,\qquad \|k_1\|\le j_n^2,\\ \sum_{\nu<\ell}\|k_{\nu+1}-k_\nu\| \le(C_K\eta+\epsilon_n)N. \end{gathered} \label{links:selected-rows}$$ Rows can be held across omitted columns without increasing their variation.* 4. *Every retained piece obeys the charged-tunnel bound $$(c_i^{\rm cost})^-\le Y_{z_i,t_i}+E_{z_i}. \label{links:tunnel-bound}$$ Here $Y$ is the local saving of Section 6.5, and $E$ is a fixed local sum at the piece center that dominates both selected endpoint errors for every allowed piece. The finite phase-template fields for $Y$ satisfy Proposition <a href="#access:collection" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="access:collection">47</a>; those for $E$ have fixed range and tail $C_K\min(1,t^{-m_*})$.* *Set every selected list and count, including $m_N,R,\mathcal I,\mathcal L$, to the empty or zero value off $\Omega_{n,\mathfrak r}$. For finitely many link templates, apply the proposition separately, intersect their events, and take the maximum of their error sequences and the sum of their failure sequences.
  - Explanation: Metric control and extreme-point concentration supply selected cuts of a long geodesic. Halo removal, shared endpoint data, and a fixed integer-walk scan extract increasing distinct-column links while controlling irregular pieces, row variation, and charged negative costs.
- **claim-asymmetric-capped-links** (bound, [source](#stmt-links-asymmetric)): For each fixed $0<M<\infty$ and $\zeta>0$, there are $1\le J<\infty$, fixed geometric tolerances and $n_0$ such that, for every admissible $n\ge n_0$, $$\mathbb E f_{J,M}(X/\beta)\le\zeta. \label{links:eq-one}$$ The tolerances can be imposed by taking the rational $v,w$ sufficiently close to the endpoints of the flat. The choices are uniform over input road laws satisfying the stated local estimates and the sublinear upper bound for $\beta$.
  - Explanation: Thin-diagram tail control, sparse negative-link flags, and concentration along selected rows make capped mean link cost arbitrarily small. The lower cap is chosen after the prescribed upper cap.
- **claim-matched-dyadic-caps** (construction, [source](#stmt-links-matched)): Let $X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(r)}$ be finitely many required row-link templates, and let $U_1,\ldots,U_p$ be additional nonnegative local variables with a uniform bound on the sum of their first moments. For every $\zeta>0$ and every prescribed lower bound $M_{\rm prescribed}$, there is a fixed finite dyadic set $\mathcal M=\{M_0,2M_0,\ldots,2^{H-1}M_0\}$, with $M_0\ge M_{\rm prescribed}$, and fixed geometric tolerances, such that for every sufficiently large $n$ some deterministic law-dependent $M\in\mathcal M$ satisfies, simultaneously, $$\begin{aligned} \mathbb E f_{M,M}(X^{(a)}/\beta)&\le\zeta &&(1\le a\le r),\label{links:matched-mean}\\ M\left[\sum_{a=1}^r\mathbb P((X^{(a)}/\beta)^->M) +\sum_{b=1}^p\mathbb P(U_b>M)\right]&\le\zeta. \label{links:matched-tail} \end{aligned}$$ In particular $U_1$ may be the positive part of the normalized primary increment used in the road improvement.
  - Explanation: A deterministic cap from a fixed finite dyadic menu controls both symmetric clipped means and threshold-weighted tail probabilities. All concentration estimates are established for the menu before its law-dependent level is selected.
- **claim-local-primary-cost-replacement** (construction, [source](#stmt-improvement-replacement)): For the stationary local fields and compatible physical pieces constructed above, assume <a href="#improvement:primary:eq2" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="improvement:primary:eq2">[improvement:primary:eq2]</a>, <a href="#improvement:transitions:eq3" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="improvement:transitions:eq3">[improvement:transitions:eq3]</a>–<a href="#improvement:transitions:eq4" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="improvement:transitions:eq4">[improvement:transitions:eq4]</a>, and the stated independence at distances greater than $R$. There is a stationary finite-range rule selecting disjoint replacement intervals. It concatenates primary pieces, successful transitions, and spare pieces. Charge each retained primary cost to its own slot and each replacement’s total normalized corrected cost to its leftmost flag. The resulting integrable local charge $Z_i^{\mathrm{out}}$ satisfies $$\mathbb E Z_0^{\mathrm{out}} \le \mathbb EW_0+H_*Mp +C_0\{2G_*p+2(L_*+1)\delta\} +(H_*C_V+2K_\delta)p. \label{improvement:flags:eq8}$$ The range of the rule depends on $R$ and $T_*$, independently of $M$, $\delta$, and $K_\delta$.
  - Explanation: A finite-window flag-cluster rule replaces accepted short clusters using forward transitions and an independent spare baseline. Remote flags and failed tests control uncovered large costs using first moments without assuming positive-tail uniform integrability.
- **claim-road-infimum-contraction** (bound, [source](#stmt-improvement-contraction-proposition)): For suitable fixed rational $v,w$ near the flat endpoints and $s>0$, there are an integer $D\ge1$ and $\rho<1$ such that $$b(Dn)\le\rho b(n)$$ for every sufficiently large admissible $n$. The infimum on both sides uses the road class of Definition <a href="#def:fb-road" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:fb-road">21</a>, with costs in their original units.
  - Explanation: Structural tracking and support bounds determine a fixed rescaling before cap and probability tolerances. The improved roads return to the original admissible class and contract its period-bound infimum without requiring an attained minimizer.
- **claim-fixed-direction-geodesics** (theorem, [source](#stmt-cor-fixed-direction)): Fix a deterministic unit vector $u$. There is an event $\Omega_u$ of probability one on which all the following statements hold.* 1. *For every $x\in\mathbb Z^2$ there is exactly one infinite geodesic $\Gamma_x^u$ from $x$ with direction $u$. For every sequence $(z_n)$ directed toward $u$, including a sequence chosen from the edge configuration, $\Gamma(x,z_n)\to\Gamma_x^u$ locally.* 2. *For every $x,y\in\mathbb Z^2$, the paths $\Gamma_x^u$ and $\Gamma_y^u$ have a common tail.* 3. *No bigeodesic has an end with direction $u$.* 4. *For every $x,y\in\mathbb Z^2$, the limit $$B_u(x,y)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\bigl(T(x,z_n)-T(y,z_n)\bigr)$$ exists and is independent of the choice of sequence directed toward $u$. Moreover, $$\mathbb EB_u(0,x)=\nabla\mu(u)\cdot x,$$ and, for every $\varepsilon>0$, only finitely many $x\in\mathbb Z^2$ satisfy $$\|B_u(0,x)-\nabla\mu(u)\cdot x\|>\varepsilon\lVert x\rVert_1.$$
  - Explanation: For a prescribed deterministic direction in the exponential model, a common probability-one event gives directed-ray uniqueness, convergence from all directed target sequences, coalescence, directional bigeodesic exclusion, and a sequence-independent Busemann limit with the stated mean and asymptotic control.
- **claim-qualitative-midpoint-decay** (bound, [source](#stmt-cor-midpoint)): For every nonzero $v\in\mathbb Z^2$, $$\lim_{n\to\infty} \mathbb P\bigl(\lfloor n/2\rfloor v\in\Gamma(0,nv)\bigr)=0.$$ More generally, let $a_n,b_n,z_n$ be deterministic lattice vertices with $$\lVert a_n-z_n\rVert_2\to\infty, \quad\lVert b_n-z_n\rVert_2\to\infty, \quad \frac{b_n-z_n}{\lVert b_n-z_n\rVert_2}\longrightarrow u$$ for a deterministic unit vector $u$. Then $\mathbb P(z_n\in\Gamma(a_n,b_n))\to0$.
  - Explanation: A positive limiting probability of passage through a prescribed escaping midpoint would yield a bigeodesic by local compactness. The fixed-direction exclusion rules out that event for the stated deterministic endpoint sequences.
- **claim-gamma-quantitative-midpoint** (bound, [source](#stmt-cor-gamma-quantitative-midpoint)): For every $\kappa>0$ there is $C_\kappa<\infty$ such that, for every $\lambda>0$ and all $a,b,z\in\mathbb Z^2$ with $D=\min\{\lVert a-z\rVert_1,\lVert b-z\rVert_1\}\geq1$, $$\mathbb P\bigl(z\in\Gamma_{\kappa,\lambda}(a,b)\bigr) \leq C_\kappa\frac{\log^2(D+2)}{D^{1/16}},$$ where $\Gamma_{\kappa,\lambda}$ denotes the unique geodesic for iid $\operatorname{Gamma}(\kappa,\lambda)$ edge weights.
  - Explanation: Gamma differentiability implies infinitely many extreme points, enabling the cited quantitative midpoint theorem. Scaling every weight by the same positive rate factor leaves geodesics unchanged, so the constant depends on shape but not rate.
- **claim-gamma-cone-tip-survival** (classification, [source](#stmt-cor-gamma-cone-tip)): Fix $\kappa,\lambda>0$, a deterministic unit vector $\theta\in S^1$, and a geometric half-angle $0\le\alpha\le\pi$. Define the closed cone $$\begin{aligned} C^\theta_\alpha&=\{0\}\cup \{x\in\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\}:\angle(x,-\theta)\le\alpha\},\\ I_1&=(C^\theta_\alpha\cap\mathbb Z^2)\setminus\{0\}, \qquad I_2=\{0\}, \end{aligned}$$ where $\angle(x,-\theta)$ is the Euclidean angle between the two vectors. Use one iid $\operatorname{Gamma}(\kappa,\lambda)$ field on unoriented nearest-neighbor edges of $\mathbb Z^2$, with passage metric $T$. At time zero, start type 1 from every site of $I_1$ and type 2 from $I_2$. Both types use this same realization of $T$, and each site is permanently claimed by the type that reaches it first. With $T(I,z)=\inf_{x\in I}T(x,z)$, interpreting the infimum of the empty set as $\infty$, the sites eventually claimed by type 2 are almost surely $$\mathcal E_2=\{z\in\mathbb Z^2:T(0,z)<T(I_1,z)\}.$$ Then $$\mathbb P\bigl(\|\mathcal E_2\|=\infty\bigr)>0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \alpha<\pi/2.$$ In particular, at $\alpha=\pi/2$, when the cone is the closed half-plane $\{x:x\cdot\theta\le0\}$, type 2 claims only finitely many sites almost surely. At $\kappa=1$, this gives Benjamini’s cone-tip prediction for equal-rate Richardson competition with any common rate $\lambda>0$ in the same initial configuration.
  - Explanation: For simultaneous cone-versus-tip growth using one shared Gamma passage metric, positive tip survival occurs precisely below the critical geometric half-angle. At the critical half-plane and larger cones the tip claims finitely many sites almost surely; exponential weights give the equal-rate Richardson specialization.

```json
        "anchor": "stmt-found-lem-network",
        "exact_quote": "Let $A=v+sw$, $B=w+sv$ with $0<s<1/4$, and suppose two road rules have tracking radius $r$ and dependence radius $10$ in $\\|\\cdot\\|_*$, and expected defect at most $\\beta$ on each marked unit period. Here an input cell contains all microscopic weights and private inputs assigned to the corresponding unit parallelogram.*\n\n*One may also prescribe any collection of additional marked anchors $X_{z,\\lambda}$, each on a translated $A$- or $B$-road within a fixed distance of $z_1A+z_2B$.         "anchor": "stmt-found-lem-envelope",
        "exact_quote": "Fix $m$ road labels and parameter windows of length at most $L$ contained in a bounded macroscopic neighborhood of a deterministic cell. There is a nonnegative local random variable $U$ with $\\mathbb EU\\leq C_{m,L}\\beta$ which bounds all of the following: absolute corrected signed costs within these windows; sums with a bounded number of switches between these labels at intersections; and the gauge differences for such switches at their common physical vertex. The support radius depends only on $L$, the neighborhood size, and the original road locality radius.*\n\n*If a physical path is confined to a prescribed deterministic finite closed metric subgraph and has endpoints on two of the windows, its corrected cost, including signed adjustments to prescribed center anchors, is bounded below by $-U'$ for a local nonnegative variable $U'$ with $\\mathbb EU'\\leq C_{m,L}\\beta$. Its support also includes the prescribed subgraph. This bound holds simultaneously for every such path and every choice of its endpoints.",

        "exact_quote": "Suppose the period excess bound satisfies $\\beta\\leq C_s n^\\alpha$ for some fixed $\\alpha<1$.         "exact_quote": "Fix deterministic tubes and a baseline road contained in one of them. Write $\\eta=(\\eta_0,\\eta_{\\rm other})$ for all preserved tube weights, where $\\eta_0$ consists exactly of the weights in the baseline’s own tube and $\\eta_{\\rm other}$ contains the remaining preserved edges. Let $\\xi$ contain the baseline’s private road seeds and a private completion of the entire complement of its own tube. Construct the baseline once, using the actual weights in its own tube and these private inputs everywhere else. The resulting road is a function of $(\\eta_0,\\xi)$ alone.*\n\n*In each world $j$, retain all prescribed tube weights and use an iid completion $\\zeta^j$ elsewhere. For every $j$, the private input $\\xi$ is independent of the joint tuple $(\\eta,\\zeta^j)$; different worlds may share coordinates with one another. Assume that every world has the correct product weight law, uses the same measurable calibration map, and supplies the local comparison network above with period bound $\\beta$. Assume also that the shared baseline is admissible in every world and has expected defect at most $\\beta$ on each marked period there. The latter condition follows from the random-cut period identity when the shared baseline rule has period excess at most $\\beta$.*\n\n\n*Let $g_x^j$ be the gauge given by <a href=\"#found:eq-gauge-formula\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"found:eq-gauge-formula\">[found:eq-gauge-formula]</a> at a marked baseline anchor. After interpolation along any bounded baseline interval, the same assertion holds with an expected supremum bound of order $\\beta$.         "exact_quote": "A fixed bounded region contains at most $J$ candidate cells. There is a local random variable $V$ that bounds, simultaneously for every object, its smallest available $U_c$, and satisfies $$\\mathbb P(V>t)\\le J^m\\min\\{1,(A/t)^m\\},\\qquad t>0.$$ For fixed $J,m,A$, the fourth moment of $V$ is uniformly bounded when $m>4$. Suppose also that their distinct sites can be visited by a path whose initial distance from the origin plus total length is at most $c(N+1)$.*\n\n\n*For every $F\\ge1$ there is $C_F<\\infty$ such that, for $T\\ge1$ and $0\\le\\delta\\le F^{-2}$, $$\\mathbb E\\sup_{S\\in\\mathcal S(N,\\delta)}\n       \\sum_{z\\in S}Y_z\\mathbf1_{\\{Y_z>T\\}}\n \\le \\frac{CN}{F}+\\frac{C_F(N+1)}{T}+C_F.\n \\label{probability:thin-tail-bound}$$ Here $C$ is independent of $F,T,\\delta,n$.       },

        "anchor": "stmt-probability-rows",
        "exact_quote": "For each $n$, let $W^{(n)}_{i,j}$, $i,j\\in\\mathbb Z$, be real random variables with $|W^{(n)}_{i,j}|\\le B$. Suppose that for every deterministic sequence $(j_i)$, the variables $(W^{(n)}_{i,j_i})$ in each residue class $i\\pmod q$ are mutually independent. The integer $q\\ge1$ and $B<\\infty$ are fixed. One sufficient condition is mutual independence of the sigma-fields generated by entire columns in any set of columns separated by at least $q$.*\n\n\n*Fix $d<\\infty$ and $\\varepsilon>0$. Consider rows with $|j_1|\\le N^d$ and $\\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}|j_{i+1}-j_i|\\le\\delta N$, and omission sets $O\\subset\\{1,\\ldots,N\\}$ with $|O|\\le\\eta N$. For sufficiently small fixed $\\delta,\\eta>0$, depending only on $\\varepsilon,B,q,d$, uniformly in $n$, $$\\mathbb P\\left(\n  \\sup_{(j_i),O}\\left|\n    \\sum_{i\\notin O}\\big(W^{(n)}_{i,j_i}\n                         -\\mathbb EW^{(n)}_{i,j_i}\\big)\n                        \\right|>\\varepsilon N\\right)\n \\longrightarrow0\\qquad(N\\to\\infty).\n \\label{probability:row-concentration}$$ The convergence is exponential up to a polynomial factor. If all means equal $m_n$, the comparison sum is $m_n(N-|O|)$. The conclusion applies to indicators and to bounded sums over any fixed finite list of offsets or types that separately satisfy the hypotheses, with adjusted constants. A direct application to the sum requires independence at a spacing $q$ appropriate to its combined input supports.",

        "anchor": "stmt-links-halos",
        "exact_quote": "Let $x_0,\\ldots,x_m$ be successive cuts of a path. All distances in this lemma use the $(A,B)$ maximum norm. Suppose $K/2\\le|x_{i+1}-x_i|\\le CK$, and associate to each starting cut $x_i$ a center $z_i$ within a fixed distance $H_0$, independent of the cone enlargement. Suppose, for $c_*>0$ and $\\epsilon_n^{\\rm raw}\\to0$, its raw costs satisfy $$Q_i\\ge-\\epsilon_n^{\\rm raw}n\\quad\\hbox{for all }i,\n \\qquad Q_i\\ge c_*n\\quad\\hbox{for bad }i.$$ Let effective cut labels satisfy $|\\widetilde g_i-g_{\\rm ref}|\\le\\lambda n$ for one common constant $g_{\\rm ref}$. For sufficiently small $\\lambda>0$ there is a set $R$ of removed indices containing all bad indices, of cardinality at most a fixed multiple of their number, for which*\n\n1.  *$\\sum_{i\\in R}(Q_i-\\widetilde g_{i+1}+\\widetilde g_i)\\ge0$;*\n\n2.  *retained centers $z_i$ are in $\\mathcal C_2$-order up to a bounded additive error, for every pair of retained indices;*\n\n3.  *the same order includes the initial and terminal points, up to a bounded additive error;*\n\n4.  *repetitions of any one center have bounded multiplicity, independently of how small the cone enlargement is.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-links-extraction",
        "exact_quote": "For every sufficiently small fixed $\\delta,\\eta>0$, the final geometric choices above can be made so that there are deterministic $\\epsilon_n,\\pi_n\\to0$ and fixed constants $H,C,C_K,c>0$ and integers $q_K,m_0$ with the following property. For each $\\mathfrak r\\in\\mathfrak R_n$ there is an event $\\Omega_{n,\\mathfrak r}$ such that $$\\sup_{\\mathfrak r\\in\\mathfrak R_n}\n \\mathbb P_{\\mathfrak r}(\\Omega_{n,\\mathfrak r}^{\\,c})\\le\\pi_n.\n \\label{links:extraction-event}$$ Let $x_n^\\star$ be a deterministic nearest vertex of $\\mathcal G_n$ to $Na$, and put $$j_n=\\left\\lfloor u(x_n^\\star)/d+\\tfrac12\\right\\rfloor,\\qquad\n \\mathcal J_n=\\{0,1,\\ldots,j_n-1\\}.$$ For large $n$, $cN\\le j_n\\le CN$. On $\\Omega_{n,\\mathfrak r}$, a geodesic from $0$ to $x_n^\\star$ has consecutive selected pieces $\\gamma_i:x_i\\to x_{i+1}$, $0\\le i<m_N$, after two bounded terminal fragments are removed, and the following objects and bounds.*\n\n\n1.  *There are at most $CN/K+C$ pieces, each of diameter $O(K)$, with consecutive cut displacement between $K/2$ and $2K$ in the $(A,B)$ maximum norm. The shared data in <a href=\"#links:piece-cost\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"links:piece-cost\">[links:piece-cost]</a> have $|\\widetilde g_i-g_{\\rm ref}|\\le\\lambda n$. A removed set $R$ contains every bad piece of Lemma <a href=\"#links:halos\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"links:halos\">49</a> and satisfies $$|R|\\le\\epsilon_nN,\\qquad\n     \\sum_{i\\in R}c_i^{\\rm cost}\\ge0,\\qquad\n     \\sum_{i\\notin R}c_i^{\\rm cost}\\le\\epsilon_nN.\n     \\label{links:retained-cost}$$*\n\n\n2.  *The retained pieces have types $t_i$ from the fixed access family and centers $z_i$ on its fixed finite family of full-rank center lattices, after bounded rounding. Let $E=[e_1\\ e_2]$, where the $e_j$ are the boundary generators of $\\mathcal C_2$, normalized by $h(e_j)=1$ and ordered so that $e_1\\to a$ and $e_2\\to b$ as $\\mathcal C_2$ shrinks to $\\mathcal C$. In chronological order the centers satisfy $$E^{-1}(z_j-z_i)\\ge-H(1,1)\\quad(i<j),\\qquad\n     z_i\\in E([-H,CN+H]\\times[-H,\\delta N+H]).\n     \\label{links:retained-geometry}$$ The inequality is coordinatewise. Each rounded site occurs at most $m_0$ times, and the initial distance from the origin plus total successive center distance is at most $C(N+1)$. These bounds persist on every type and sparse-residue subsequence. The matrices $E$ range in a fixed compact family, and $H,C,m_0$ remain bounded when the final cone is narrowed.*\n\n\n\n3.  *An irregular retained set $\\mathcal I$ has $|\\mathcal I|\\le(C_K\\eta+\\epsilon_n)N$. Each $i\\notin R\\cup\\mathcal I$ supplies at most $q_K$ admissible links $\\mathcal L_i$, with $$c_i^{\\rm cost}\\ge\\sum_{(j,k)\\in\\mathcal L_i}X_{j,k}/\\beta.\n     \\label{links:unclipped-comparison}$$ In the chronological list $\\mathcal L=\\bigcup_{i\\notin R\\cup\\mathcal I}\\mathcal L_i$, columns are distinct, increasing, and belong to $\\mathcal J_n$. For sufficiently small fixed $\\eta$, $|\\mathcal L|\\ge cN$ for all large $n$, after decreasing $c$ once. If $k_1,\\ldots,k_\\ell$ are the selected rows, then $$\\begin{gathered}\n     |\\mathcal J_n\\setminus\\{j:(j,k)\\in\\mathcal L\\}|\n           \\le(C_K\\eta+\\epsilon_n)N,\\qquad |k_1|\\le j_n^2,\\\\\n     \\sum_{\\nu<\\ell}|k_{\\nu+1}-k_\\nu|\n           \\le(C_K\\eta+\\epsilon_n)N.\n     \\end{gathered}\n     \\label{links:selected-rows}$$ Rows can be held across omitted columns without increasing their variation.*\n\n\n4.  *Every retained piece obeys the charged-tunnel bound $$(c_i^{\\rm cost})^-\\le Y_{z_i,t_i}+E_{z_i}.\n     \\label{links:tunnel-bound}$$ Here $Y$ is the local saving of Section 6.5, and $E$ is a fixed local sum at the piece center that dominates both selected endpoint errors for every allowed piece. The finite phase-template fields for $Y$ satisfy Proposition <a href=\"#access:collection\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"access:collection\">47</a>; those for $E$ have fixed range and tail $C_K\\min(1,t^{-m_*})$.*\n\n*Set every selected list and count, including $m_N,R,\\mathcal I,\\mathcal L$, to the empty or zero value off $\\Omega_{n,\\mathfrak r}$. For finitely many link templates, apply the proposition separately, intersect their events, and take the maximum of their error sequences and the sum of their failure sequences.",

        "anchor": "stmt-links-matched",
        "exact_quote": "Let $X^{(1)},\\ldots,X^{(r)}$ be finitely many required row-link templates, and let $U_1,\\ldots,U_p$ be additional nonnegative local variables with a uniform bound on the sum of their first moments. For every $\\zeta>0$ and every prescribed lower bound $M_{\\rm prescribed}$, there is a fixed finite dyadic set $\\mathcal M=\\{M_0,2M_0,\\ldots,2^{H-1}M_0\\}$, with $M_0\\ge M_{\\rm prescribed}$, and fixed geometric tolerances, such that for every sufficiently large $n$ some deterministic law-dependent $M\\in\\mathcal M$ satisfies, simultaneously, $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\mathbb E f_{M,M}(X^{(a)}/\\beta)&\\le\\zeta\n       &&(1\\le a\\le r),\\label{links:matched-mean}\\\\\n M\\left[\\sum_{a=1}^r\\mathbb P((X^{(a)}/\\beta)^->M)\n       +\\sum_{b=1}^p\\mathbb P(U_b>M)\\right]&\\le\\zeta.\n \\label{links:matched-tail}\n\\end{aligned}$$ In particular $U_1$ may be the positive part of the normalized primary increment used in the road improvement.",
        "source_id": "PM-212.2"
      },
```

<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Passage time** ([source](#sec:introduction)): Then $$T(x,y)=\inf_{P:x\to y}\tau(P)$$ is its passage time.
- **Path traversal cost** ([source](#sec:introduction)): The cost $\tau(P)$ of a finite path is the sum of its edge weights, counted with traversal multiplicity.
- **Path displacement** ([source](#sec:introduction)): Write $\Delta P$ for its terminal vertex minus its initial vertex.
- **Limit shape** ([source](#sec:introduction)): Its unit ball $\mathcal B=\{v:\mu(v)\le1\}$ is the limit shape.
- **Supporting-functional path defect** ([source](#df:eq:minimum-defect)): The *defect* of a path is its cost minus the value of a supporting functional on its displacement.
- **Allowed strip-crossing event** ([source](#pm-h-13)): For real $s\geq1$ and integer $n\geq1$, let $E(s,n)$ be the event that there is a finite path $P$ from the column $x=0$ to the column $x=n$, with every vertex in $$\{-n\leq x\leq2n,\ \left\lvert r\right\rvert\leq8s\},$$ and with $$\tau(P)<m_0n+Ks.$$
- **Full path chunk** ([source](#df:wi:chunk-index)): A chunk ending at such a cut is called *full*.
- **Admissible road** ([source](#stmt-def-fb-road)): For $d\in\{A,B\}$, an admissible $d$-road is a measurable oriented two-sided lattice walk together with a continuous nondecreasing nominal parameter on its edge occurrences.
- **Common road-period bound** ([source](#sec:fb-roads)): $$ The first term has mean zero; the second has the law of $P_n(X_0)$. All terms are integrable because each cut lies on one of finitely many deterministic edges, where domination bounds its calibration value by a finite sum of weights and a deterministic linear term. Taking expectations proves the first identity, and <a href="#eq:fb-defect" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:fb-defect">[eq:fb-defect]</a> proves the second. The mean of $P_n(X_0)$ itself need not vanish. ◻ </details> For a pair of admissible roads define its common period bound as $$\beta=\max\bigl\{ \mathbb EQ_n(\gamma_A[0,1]), \mathbb EQ_n(\gamma_B[0,1])\bigr\},$$ and let $b(n)$ be the infimum over admissible pairs.
- **Nonnegative cocycle defect** ([source](#eq:fb-defect)): For a path $\gamma$ from $x$ to $y$, put $$P_n(x)=B_n(0,x)-nh(x),\qquad Q_n(\gamma)=\tau(\gamma)-nh(y-x)$$ and define its *defect* by $$D_n(\gamma) =Q_n(\gamma)-P_n(y)+P_n(x) =\tau(\gamma)-B_n(x,y)\ge0. \label{eq:fb-defect}$$
- **Interpolated road gauge** ([source](#found:eq-interpolation)): For an occurrence between the marked cuts $i$ and $i+1$, with nominal parameter $t\in[i,i+1]$, set $$g(t)=g_i+Q(i,t)-(t-i)C_i. \label{found:eq-interpolation}$$
- **Center-label internal cost** ([source](#access:center-cost)): The internal cost measured at center labels is $$\label{access:center-cost} H(\pi)=C_{W_-}(x_0,x)+C_\pi(x,y)+C_{W_+}(y,y_0).$$
- **Charged tunnel reward** ([source](#access:charge)): Charge their conditional expected cost: $$\label{access:charge} a_{\mathcal D} =\beta^{-1}\mathbb E[U_{c_-}+U_{c_+}\mid\mathcal F_{\mathcal D}], \qquad Y=(u-a_{\mathcal D})_+,$$
- **Minimum signed horizontal link** ([source](#links:definition)): Measure the crossing at the two row centers by setting $$\begin{aligned} L_{j,k}(\gamma) &=C_j(c_{j,k},x) +Q_n(\gamma)-g_{j+1}(x')+g_j(x) +C_{j+1}(x',c_{j+1,k}), \\ X_{j,k}&=\min_\gamma L_{j,k}(\gamma). \label{links:definition} \end{aligned}$$
- **Asymmetric clipping** ([source](#links:master)): For $J,M>0$, write $f_{J,M}(x)=\max(-J,\min(x,M))$.
- **Finite and infinite geodesics** ([source](#pm-h-76)): A finite geodesic is a path realizing the passage time between its endpoints. An infinite geodesic, or a bigeodesic, is respectively a one-sided or two-sided infinite path every finite segment of which is a finite geodesic.
- **Directed target sequence** ([source](#pm-h-76)): A sequence $(z_n)$ is directed toward a unit vector $u$ when $\lVert z_n\rVert_2\to\infty$ and $z_n/\lVert z_n\rVert_2\to u$.
- **Local convergence of rooted paths** ([source](#pm-h-76)): Local convergence of paths rooted at $x$ means eventual agreement of each fixed finite initial segment.
