<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-gamma-moments** [claim](#stmt-df-ga-moment) / [proof](#proof-stmt-df-ga-moment): Integrate the density, then apply independence and exponential Markov inequality. -> Exponential moments and attachment-cost tails.
- **step-extreme-supports** [claim](#stmt-df-prelim-supports) / [proof](#proof-stmt-df-prelim-supports): Use convex subgradients, homogeneity, and extension from positive longitudinal coordinates. -> Global supporting functionals with one-sided contact.
- **step-local-travel** [claim](#stmt-df-cr-local-travel) / [proof](#proof-stmt-df-cr-local-travel): Subdivide the joining segment, apply uniform shape and escape estimates, and concatenate short confined paths. -> High-probability localized travel uniform over deterministic endpoints.
- **step-interval-travel** [claim](#stmt-df-cr-interval-travel) / [proof](#proof-stmt-df-cr-interval-travel): Use deterministic endpoint nets and whole-gap vertical cost bounds. -> A common event connecting all interval endpoint pairs.
- **step-oriented-good-path** [claim](#stmt-df-cr-oriented-paths) / [proof](#proof-stmt-df-cr-oriented-paths): If reachability is finite, extract a winding contour and sum probabilities of its separated bad sites. -> Positive probability of an infinite good oriented path.
- **step-fast-crossing-contradiction** [claim](#stmt-df-cr-rare-fast) / [proof](#proof-stmt-df-cr-rare-fast): Amplify independent strip trials, connect them on the contact side, and contradict the origin shape theorem. -> Joint-limit rarity of negative-defect strip crossings.
- **step-cubic-tilt** [claim](#stmt-df-gr-tilt) / [proof](#proof-stmt-df-gr-tilt): Scale finitely many Gamma weights and compute the likelihood second moment before Cauchy–Schwarz transfer. -> Allowed crossings are rare at cubic length.
- **step-characteristic-threshold** [claim](#stmt-df-gr-characteristic-lengths) / [proof](#proof-stmt-df-gr-characteristic-lengths): Prove short crossings likely and take the first dyadic probability threshold. -> Characteristic lengths with an upper bound and diverging width ratio.
- **step-record-minima** [claim](#stmt-df-gr-record-scales) / [proof](#proof-stmt-df-gr-record-scales): Take strict record minima of the rescaled positive characteristic-length sequence. -> Infinite scale subsequence compatible with earlier meshes.
- **step-grid-connections** [claim](#stmt-df-gr-grid-tools) / [proof](#proof-stmt-df-gr-grid-tools): Run separated translated crossing trials, bound vertical attachments, and sum over all tested mesh bins. -> Simultaneous grid connections with summable errors.
- **step-arbitrary-endpoints** [claim](#stmt-df-gr-variable-endpoints) / [proof](#proof-stmt-df-gr-variable-endpoints): Attach every endpoint to coarse columns with nested meshes and then test finitely many coarse crossings. -> Negative-defect rarity for arbitrary observed endpoints.
- **step-continuous-bk** [claim](#stmt-df-wi-continuous-bk) / [proof](#proof-stmt-df-wi-continuous-bk): Round quantiles from above into finite independent bits and pass strict path witnesses to the limit. -> Product bound for disjoint path witnesses, including repeated event labels.
- **step-chunk-witness** [claim](#stmt-df-wi-chunk-witness) / [proof](#proof-stmt-df-wi-chunk-witness): Check transverse, backward longitudinal, and forward longitudinal exits at one fixed scale. -> Every cheap full chunk contains a local event witness.
- **step-witness-multiplicity** [claim](#stmt-df-wi-chunk-defect) / [proof](#proof-stmt-df-wi-chunk-defect): Split successive negative prefixes and bound each split's overshoot using the single-step defect bound. -> Chunk and whole-path defect lower bounds in terms of witness multiplicity.
- **step-long-path-counting** [claim](#stmt-df-wi-long-paths) / [proof](#proof-stmt-df-wi-long-paths): Count deterministic itineraries and witness allocations, apply BK, and invoke Borel–Cantelli. -> Almost-sure eventual linear defect for all long simple paths.
- **step-exclude-corner** [claim](#stmt-df-wi-no-corner) / [proof](#proof-stmt-df-wi-no-corner): Compare approximate minimizers along the contact direction with the fixed-scale long-path defect bound. -> Agreement of one-sided transverse derivatives for every deterministic direction.
- **step-convex-regularity** [claim](#stmt-df-convex-regularity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-df-convex-regularity): Identify one-sided derivatives with extreme supports, prove continuity by dual compactness, and apply the implicit function theorem. -> Equivalence of differentiability, unique supporting lines, and regular boundary.
- **step-gamma-main-theorem** [claim](#stmt-thm-gamma-differentiability) / [proof](#proof-stmt-df-convex-regularity-2): Combine no-corner directions with signed coordinate symmetries, homogeneity, and convex regularity. -> Gamma norm differentiability and continuously differentiable boundary.
- **step-metric-estimates** [claim](#stmt-model-metric) / [proof](#proof-stmt-model-metric): Use cited mean and concentration estimates, union bounds over polynomial boxes, and incident-edge corrections. -> Uniform sublinear metric errors and integrated lower deficits.
- **step-random-cut-means** [claim](#stmt-lem-fb-random-cuts) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-fb-random-cuts): Apply joint stationarity, centered cocycle additivity, and covariant marked cuts. -> Equality of expected defect and raw period excess.
- **step-cheap-path-counting** [claim](#stmt-lem-fb-cheap-paths) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-fb-cheap-paths): Count self-avoiding paths and compare geodesics with a coordinate path. -> Long-cheap-path bound and exponential geodesic-length tails.
- **step-road-initialization** [claim](#stmt-prop-fb-upper) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-fb-upper): Concatenate restricted minimizing paths between deterministic close anchors. -> Admissible road pairs with sublinear period excess.
- **step-positive-road-infimum** [claim](#stmt-prop-fb-positive) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-fb-positive): Decrease weights in a middle region used by one route, then transfer a competitor saving through total variation. -> Strictly positive common period-bound infimum.
- **step-local-comparison-network** [claim](#stmt-found-lem-network) / [proof](#proof-stmt-found-lem-network): Choose planar intersection occurrences and join anchors by bounded signed trips. -> Local approximate calibration increments.
- **step-finite-cell-gauges** [claim](#stmt-found-lem-finite-cell) / [proof](#proof-stmt-found-lem-finite-cell): Use finite-product projections with deterministic cutoffs and connected exterior detours. -> Local mean-matching potentials with controlled increment errors.
- **step-local-envelopes** [claim](#stmt-found-lem-envelope) / [proof](#proof-stmt-found-lem-envelope): Interpolate anchor gauges and take local suprema and extrema over bounded occurrence windows. -> Uniform corrected-cost and competitor lower envelopes.
- **step-gauge-linear-tails** [claim](#stmt-found-lem-gauge-tail) / [proof](#proof-stmt-found-lem-gauge-tail): Estimate raw-cost and gauge suprema using metric deficits, finite projections, and Markov inequality. -> Sublinear absolute-gauge expectations and linear-scale tails.
- **step-common-baseline-gauge** [claim](#stmt-found-lem-common-gauge) / [proof](#proof-stmt-found-lem-common-gauge): Replace projected calibration increments by shared baseline costs and compare exterior detours separately in each world. -> Local incoming gauge common to all eligible worlds.
- **step-phase-locality** [claim](#stmt-phases-locality) / [proof](#proof-stmt-phases-locality): Track finite phase lists through both gauge anchors and average over deterministic offsets. -> Translation covariance and independence of separated entire columns.
- **step-sparse-indicator-lists** [claim](#stmt-probability-sparse) / [proof](#proof-stmt-probability-sparse): Count marked-site lists under a travel budget and sum over independence classes. -> Uniform sparse-path expectation bound.
- **step-integrated-tails** [claim](#stmt-probability-integrated-tails) / [proof](#proof-stmt-probability-integrated-tails): Move path suprema inside a nonnegative layer-cake integral and apply sparse-path bounds. -> Selected-tail expectation bound.
- **step-candidate-minima** [claim](#stmt-probability-candidates) / [proof](#proof-stmt-probability-candidates): Maximize the minimum over every separated support tuple and apply product Markov bounds. -> Local simultaneous candidate-cost domination with light tails.
- **step-lattice-permutation** [claim](#stmt-probability-matching) / [proof](#proof-stmt-probability-matching): Match positive-area tile intersections using finite Hall conditions and a diagonal compactness limit. -> Bounded-displacement bijection of the infinite lattice.
- **step-thin-geometry** [claim](#stmt-probability-thin-geometry) / [proof](#proof-stmt-probability-thin-geometry): Contract one coordinate and stretch the other, then absorb uniform matching errors. -> Compressed square and cone order for separated sites.
- **step-weak-quadratic-tail** [claim](#stmt-probability-weak-two) / [proof](#proof-stmt-probability-weak-two): Choose an independent-site square sized to the exceedance probability and use singleton collection rewards. -> Weak quadratic tail bound.
- **step-thin-tail-pruning** [claim](#stmt-probability-thin-tails) / [proof](#proof-stmt-probability-thin-tails): Separate nearby collisions from a greedily retained separated set and transport the latter into a directed chain. -> Negligible selected tails in thin diagrams.
- **step-row-entropy-concentration** [claim](#stmt-probability-rows) / [proof](#proof-stmt-probability-rows): Apply Hoeffding by column residue class and count bounded-variation rows and omission masks. -> Uniform concentration before row and omission selection.
- **step-dyadic-menu** [claim](#stmt-probability-dyadic) / [proof](#proof-stmt-probability-dyadic): Average the finite geometric sum of threshold-weighted indicators. -> Deterministic law-dependent good tail level.
- **step-conditional-access-envelope** [claim](#stmt-access-conditioning) / [proof](#proof-stmt-access-conditioning): Sum conditional expectations over all subsets of the fixed local input support. -> One local bound for every deterministic union-cell observation.
- **step-forward-access** [claim](#stmt-access-physical) / [proof](#proof-stmt-access-physical): Choose exterior intersections beyond observed faces and telescope signed center arms inside actual forward attachments. -> Physical realization of center-label cost with bounded extra access.
- **step-selected-cut-tuples** [claim](#stmt-access-selected-cuts) / [proof](#proof-stmt-access-selected-cuts): Use separated annular or horizontal candidates and a common access-plus-gauge objective. -> Ordered selected cuts with simultaneous charge and gauge control.
- **step-tunnel-accounting** [claim](#stmt-access-accounting) / [proof](#proof-stmt-access-accounting): Compare with the local internal minimum and subtract the conditional forward-access charge. -> Negative-cost domination and conditional negative tunnel realization.
- **step-collection-routing** [claim](#stmt-access-collection) / [proof](#proof-stmt-access-collection): Route a maximizing observed chain through corridors whose inputs avoid every observed halo, then apply calibration domination at fixed exterior windows. -> Uniform finite-volume linear collection bound.
- **step-extreme-modulus** [claim](#stmt-links-extreme) / [proof](#proof-stmt-links-extreme): Use compactness of sphere measures and extremality of their limiting barycenter. -> Vanishing norm mass away from the endpoint direction.
- **step-density-halos** [claim](#stmt-links-halos) / [proof](#proof-stmt-links-halos): Remove maximal bad-density intervals, use forward progress on good increments, and pay gauge differences from raw penalties. -> All-pairs ordered retained centers with nonnegative removed cost.
- **step-geodesic-link-extraction** [claim](#stmt-links-extraction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-links-extraction): Combine fine direction control, selected cuts, halo masks, hysteresis rows, and a fixed running-maximum scan of the wall-index walk. -> Distinct increasing-column links and controlled irregular, geometric, and row errors.
- **step-asymmetric-link-caps** [claim](#stmt-links-asymmetric) / [proof](#proof-stmt-links-asymmetric): Combine extraction with template sparse flags, thin selected tails, and row concentration, then contradict a persistent positive capped mean. -> Small asymmetric capped means uniformly over eligible road laws.
- **step-matched-link-caps** [claim](#stmt-links-matched) / [proof](#proof-stmt-links-matched): Choose a first-moment good level from a finite menu and establish mean and flag concentration simultaneously for every level. -> A common law-dependent cap with small clipped means and weighted tails.
- **step-local-replacement** [claim](#stmt-improvement-replacement) / [proof](#proof-stmt-improvement-replacement): Test complete short flag clusters in finite windows, use successful forward transitions, and charge spare costs to nearby primary flags. -> Stationary local output-charge mean bound.
- **step-original-class-contraction** [claim](#stmt-improvement-contraction-proposition) / [proof](#proof-stmt-improvement-contraction-proposition): Verify tracking, actual-period integrability, and full input locality; fix rescaling before tolerances and pass to the infimum through approximate minimizers. -> Contraction of the original admissible-road infimum.
- **step-exponential-main-theorem** [claim](#stmt-thm-exponential-shape) / [proof](#proof-stmt-improvement-contraction-proposition-2): Iterate contraction against the positive infimum, exclude supporting segments, and combine Gamma differentiability with rate scaling. -> Strict convexity and differentiable boundary for every exponential rate.
- **step-fixed-direction-consequences** [claim](#stmt-cor-fixed-direction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-fixed-direction): Identify the supporting sector with the prescribed direction and apply the cited directional geodesic and Busemann results. -> Fixed-direction uniqueness, convergence, coalescence, Busemann limits, and directional bigeodesic exclusion.
- **step-qualitative-midpoint** [claim](#stmt-cor-midpoint) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-midpoint): Translate the tested vertex to the origin and take local limits of both geodesic arms under a positive-limsup hypothesis. -> Vanishing prescribed-vertex passage probabilities.
- **step-quantitative-gamma-midpoint** [claim](#stmt-cor-gamma-quantitative-midpoint) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-gamma-quantitative-midpoint): Deduce infinitely many extreme points from a differentiable planar boundary, invoke the cited quantitative theorem, and scale the rate. -> Shape-dependent, rate-uniform midpoint probability bound.
- **step-gamma-cone-tip** [claim](#stmt-cor-gamma-cone-tip) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-gamma-cone-tip): Check atomlessness and minimum moments, identify the tangent supporting line, apply the cone-tip theorem, and use seed-set monotonicity for the closed-cone convention. -> Sharp cone half-angle survival criterion and Richardson specialization.

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-exponential-shape-regularity**: The exponential time-constant norm is differentiable away from the origin, and its unit ball is strictly convex with a continuously differentiable boundary and unique supporting lines.
- **invariant-gamma-differentiability**: Every fixed positive-shape, positive-rate Gamma law gives a time-constant norm differentiable at every nonzero vector and a continuously differentiable limit-shape boundary.
- **invariant-fixed-direction-geodesics**: For a prescribed deterministic direction, a probability-one event supports uniqueness of directed infinite geodesics from every lattice vertex, local convergence toward them, coalescence, directional bigeodesic exclusion, and sequence-independent Busemann limits.
- **invariant-gamma-midpoint-bound**: The probability that a geodesic visits a prescribed lattice vertex obeys the stated quantitative midpoint bound, with a constant depending on Gamma shape and uniform over positive rates.
- **invariant-shared-metric-cone-tip-survival**: In the stated simultaneous cone-versus-tip initial configuration, positive probability of infinite type-2 growth occurs exactly below the critical geometric half-angle; the closed critical half-plane gives finite type-2 growth almost surely.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-gamma-strict-convexity-extension**: Treat Gamma differentiability as a proof of strict convexity for every Gamma shape. -> Unique support at a boundary point does not exclude a flat face containing several boundary points.
- **anti-directed-or-nonplanar-transfer**: Transfer the shape conclusions directly to directed routing or a nonplanar lattice. -> The model and planar intersection arguments no longer match the construction.
- **anti-simultaneous-directional-event**: Assert that the fixed-direction corollary excludes all bigeodesics or gives simultaneous uniqueness in every direction. -> The probability-one event is chosen for a prescribed direction; an uncountable intersection is not supplied.
- **anti-first-moment-selected-tail-shortcut**: Control arbitrary environment-selected tunnel rewards using only locality and a first-moment estimate. -> Selection can concentrate on large rewards, and the available weak second-moment tail does not justify the required integrated tail estimate.
- **anti-column-independence-as-spatial-independence**: Treat separated-column independence as finite dependence throughout the plane. -> A phase shared along an entire wall correlates observations along that wall.
- **anti-signed-cost-as-physical-saving**: Implement a negative signed road adjustment as a negative-cost physical reverse traversal. -> Signed center arms are additive bookkeeping; physical traversal still charges positive edge costs.
- **anti-cone-tip-model-substitution**: Use the cone-tip threshold for unequal rates, independent type-specific metrics, or competing finite seed sets. -> Those configurations change the common arrival-time comparison and initial data on which the conclusion depends.
- **anti-finite-observation-as-asymptotic-certificate**: Certify limit-shape regularity or infinite geodesic behavior from agreement on a finite simulated region. -> Finite observations do not decide the asymptotic norm, every boundary direction, or infinite-path events.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `not_applicable`. The principal results concern the deterministic norm obtained from an infinite random lattice, global boundary regularity, and infinite geodesics or survival. The introduction characterizes the norm by an almost-sure passage-time limit, and the strict-convexity proof explicitly involves the "generally nonlocal calibration $P_n$". Its road construction uses conditional expectations and asymptotic choices of scales; it does not supply a finite input-output procedure deciding these conclusions. A bounded simulation or an isolated finite auxiliary construction would therefore certify a different scope from the invariants stated here.

<a id="pm-s5"></a>
## 5. Domain engineering contracts

| domain | applies | strength | maturity | basis | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| software | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The road construction assumes random input fields, local gauges, and analytic comparison estimates. It does not supply a complete software implementation of the passage-time norm or its boundary. |
| games_simulation | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The shared-metric cone-tip model gives a mathematical specification for competing growth, but its infinite-survival conclusion provides neither a finite simulation certificate nor a stopping criterion. |
| tools | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The local optimization establishes measurable attained extrema over metric-graph paths and continuous attachment fractions. It does not specify an effective numerical representation or tolerance contract for a general optimization tool. |
| algorithms | True | moderate | adaptable | inferred | The replacement proof contains an explicit finite rule for recognizing complete short flag clusters and selecting disjoint replacement intervals. This subroutine can be implemented from supplied flags and transition-success tests; the expectation bound additionally requires the stated stochastic assumptions. |
| data_structures | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The occurrence coding distinguishes repeated visits and records continuous nominal maps. It defines measurable mathematical records, but does not establish a finite storage representation for arbitrary admissible roads. |
| hardware_accelerators | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The lattice weights model static undirected passage costs. No hardware construction identifies physical accelerator delays with these independent weights or turns asymptotic boundary smoothness into circuit timing guarantees. |
| crypto_security | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The change-of-measure argument bounds the statistical distance between perturbed exponential environments to transfer a path-saving event. It supplies no adversary model, cryptographic construction, or security reduction. |
| machine_learning | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The finite-cell potential construction uses conditional expectations under independent input cells. It does not define a learned estimator or establish generalization guarantees for dependent training data. |
| optimisation_operations_research | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The optimized quantity is an infimum over admissible random road rules under a hypothetical flat face. The contraction argument does not require an attained minimizing road and supplies no effective global optimizer for arbitrary routing problems. |
| distributed_systems | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The row estimates require independence of sufficiently separated column inputs. Shared wall phases explicitly prevent a direct inference of spatial finite dependence, and no distributed coordination protocol is constructed. |
| other | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The principal additional scope is foundational probability and convex geometry: regularity of an asymptotic norm and fixed-direction geodesic conclusions. These statements do not compute a boundary parametrization or certify all directions from finite observations. |

With $T(I,z)=\\inf_{x\\in I}T(x,z)$, interpreting the infimum of the empty set as $\\infty$, the sites eventually claimed by type 2 are almost surely $$\\mathcal E_2=\\{z\\in\\mathbb Z^2:T(0,z)<T(I_1,z)\\}.$$ Then $$\\mathbb P\\bigl(|\\mathcal E_2|=\\infty\\bigr)>0\n \\quad\\Longleftrightarrow\\quad\n \\alpha<\\pi/2.$$ In particular, at $\\alpha=\\pi/2$, when the cone is the closed half-plane $\\{x:x\\cdot\\theta\\le0\\}$, type 2 claims only finitely many sites almost surely. At $\\kappa=1$, this gives Benjamini’s cone-tip prediction for equal-rate Richardson competition with any common rate $\\lambda>0$ in the same initial configuration.",

<a id="pm-s6"></a>
## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-planar-undirected-model** (formal_scope): The shape conclusions concern undirected nearest-neighbor first-passage percolation on the planar square lattice. They do not establish corresponding results for directed paths, other graph topologies, or higher-dimensional lattices. Blocked use: ['Apply the shape theorem to directed last-passage models.', 'Transfer boundary regularity to arbitrary network graphs or nonplanar lattices.']
- **limit-fixed-independent-gamma-law** (hypothesis): Gamma differentiability requires independent edge weights with fixed positive shape and rate. The theorem does not establish differentiability for arbitrary continuous distributions or delays depending on evolving congestion. Blocked use: ['Replace the Gamma law by an arbitrary delay distribution without another proof.', 'Treat correlated or state-dependent delays as independent Gamma edge weights.']
- **limit-exponential-strict-convexity** (formal_scope): Strict convexity is proved for exponential weights. Gamma differentiability alone does not exclude a nontrivial flat face. Blocked use: ['Assert strict convexity throughout the Gamma family.', 'Identify uniqueness of a supporting line with uniqueness of its contact point.']
- **limit-origin-and-curvature** (formal_scope): The differentiability conclusion excludes the origin and gives qualitative boundary regularity. It supplies neither a formula for the limit shape nor a quantitative lower curvature bound. Blocked use: ['Assert differentiability of the norm at the origin.', 'Use the illustration as an exact boundary parametrization.', 'Infer a numerical curvature certificate from strict convexity.']
- **limit-gamma-sum-distinct-deterministic-edges** (hypothesis): The attachment-cost tail bound applies to a sum over a deterministic set of distinct independent edges with the stated edge-count budget. Repeated traversals and environment-selected edge sets need separate accounting. Blocked use: ['Treat repeated occurrences of the same edge as independent samples.', 'Apply the deterministic sum tail directly to an adaptively selected path.']
- **limit-local-travel-endpoint-selection** (hypothesis): Localized travel is uniform in deterministic endpoints. Selection after inspecting weights is justified by the separate simultaneous interval and arbitrary-endpoint constructions, with their stated geometry and scale conditions. Blocked use: ['Replace uniform probabilities for deterministic endpoint pairs by an unchecked simultaneous event for all random endpoints.', 'Use arbitrary-endpoint rarity outside the characteristic-length record subsequence.']
- **limit-characteristic-threshold-not-monotonicity** (hypothesis): Characteristic lengths are first dyadic probability thresholds. Their construction does not assume monotonicity of crossing events, and endpoint extensions use record-scale comparisons rather than a monotone length sequence. Blocked use: ['Infer crossing-event monotonicity from the definition of the first threshold.', 'Apply the endpoint-extension argument along arbitrary scales without its record comparisons.']
- **limit-strict-edge-disjoint-bk-witnesses** (hypothesis): The witness inequality requires strict deterministic cost bounds, fixed finite edge sets, and pairwise edge-disjoint witnessing paths. Overlapping event regions and repeated event labels are allowed, but overlapping witness edges are not covered. Blocked use: ['Multiply event probabilities merely because coarse boxes have distinct labels.', 'Use overlapping path certificates as disjoint witnesses.', 'Replace strict inequalities by non-strict inequalities without justifying the limiting argument.']
- **limit-corner-gap-fixed-scale-simple-paths** (hypothesis): The eventual long-path defect bound belongs to the contradiction under a positive corner gap. Its scale is fixed before path length grows, and its witness aggregation requires simple paths from the origin. Blocked use: ['Interpret the conditional positive-defect bound as an unconditional property of the differentiable norm.', 'Let the chosen scale vary during the final long-path contradiction.', 'Count repeated physical edges as disjoint witnesses.']
- **limit-road-locality-covariance-integrability** (hypothesis): The road class requires local dependence of physical weights and private inputs, tracking, covariant marked cuts, ordered occurrences, and integrable period cost. A global shared random phase or an arbitrary nonlocal routing rule is outside this class. Blocked use: ['Apply the period identity to an arbitrary random endpoint convention.', 'Admit a road whose private randomization violates locality.', 'Discard occurrence labels at repeated visits or nominal pauses.']
- **limit-random-anchor-means** (edge_case): The period identity gives a zero mean difference between covariant centered calibration values. It does not make the calibration value at an individual random cut have zero mean. Blocked use: ['Drop random endpoint corrections by asserting that every random-anchor mean vanishes.', 'Replace label means by zero in the gauge construction.']
- **limit-local-gauges-not-effective-kernels** (nonconstructive): The local-potential formula uses conditional expectations of calibration differences. Local measurability and mean matching do not supply a finite procedure for evaluating arbitrary conditional kernels or the nonlocal calibration. Blocked use: ['Treat the local gauge theorem as an executable general-purpose potential estimator.', 'Claim that locality makes exact evaluation of conditional expectations effective.']
- **limit-common-gauge-world-coupling** (hypothesis): Common incoming gauges require the prescribed product-law completions, independent baseline private inputs, the same calibration map, and baseline admissibility in every world. Gauge comparison does not identify calibrations from different worlds. Blocked use: ['Reuse the common-gauge conclusion under a biased exterior completion.', 'Equate world calibrations because their incoming tube is preserved.', "Allow shared baseline private inputs to depend on a world's actual exterior."]
- **limit-column-versus-spatial-independence** (hypothesis): Separated-column independence does not establish finite dependence throughout the plane because a wall phase is shared along its wall. Spatial selected-path estimates use compatible deterministic templates and separated product-input supports. Blocked use: ['Apply spatial sparse-path bounds directly from column independence.', 'Assume different phase-template fields are mutually independent.']
- **limit-collection-hypothesis-and-thin-geometry** (hypothesis): Critical selected-tail control requires a finite-volume collection bound in addition to locality and first moments. The thin-diagram argument also requires all-pairs order, a thin box, a travel budget, and bounded site multiplicity. Blocked use: ['Deduce negligible selected tails from local first moments alone.', 'Replace all-pairs order by bounded error in successive increments.', 'Allow uncontrolled repeated visits to one reward site.']
- **limit-weak-tail-not-second-moment** (formal_scope): The weak second-moment tail estimate does not imply a finite second moment. Direct square-root tail integration gives a divergent bound in this regime. Blocked use: ['Assert square integrability from the weak tail estimate.', 'Use the light selected-tail integral as a finite bound for the critical tunnel tail.']
- **limit-row-concentration-centering** (hypothesis): Row concentration requires bounded variables and the stated independence for every deterministic row before environment-dependent selection. After conditioning, the centering must use conditional means unless equality with unconditional means is separately established. Blocked use: ['Apply the concentration conclusion to unbounded uncapped link costs.', 'Substitute unconditional means after conditioning on shared phases without a comparison.', 'Prove concentration only for the already selected random row.']
- **limit-dyadic-cap-not-uniform-integrability** (formal_scope): The good cap is deterministic for its law and controls threshold-weighted tail probabilities. A first-moment bound and the finite cap menu do not establish uniform integrability of discarded costs. Blocked use: ['Choose the cap from the realized field while retaining the stated law-dependent estimate.', 'Infer negligible discarded-tail expectations from the good dyadic level.', 'Replace matched caps by asymmetric clipping alone in the replacement argument.']
- **limit-signed-arms-physical-access** (hypothesis): Signed center arms are bookkeeping and can have either sign. Their physical realization uses forward attachments, access charges, and gauge switches; reverse physical traversal still has positive passage cost. Blocked use: ['Implement a negative signed arm as a negative physical traversal.', 'Omit the conditional access charge when collecting tunnel rewards.', 'Condition again on the selected type instead of using its precomputed conditional charge.']
- **limit-observation-avoiding-connectors** (hypothesis): The collection proof conditions on all observations, including unused cells. Ordinary connector input supports must avoid every observed halo so that selecting a maximizing chain does not bias connector means. Blocked use: ['Check connector traces without checking their full input supports.', 'Require independence only from observations on the selected chain.', "Use uncharged access that intersects another test's observation."]
- **limit-complete-cluster-replacement-independence** (hypothesis): Replacement accepts only complete short flag clusters with successful transitions. Long and infinite clusters remain unchanged. The expectation bound additionally requires remote-test independence and independence of the entire spare and primary fields. Blocked use: ['Accept a bounded fragment of a longer cluster by inspecting only its interior.', 'Use transition success as though it were independent of spare costs.', 'Apply the expectation bound to arbitrary correlated flag and transition data.']
- **limit-contraction-original-road-class** (hypothesis): Contraction is for the same admissible road class with original cost units at both scales. Tracking, actual-period integrability, input locality, fixed parameter choices, and divisibility must survive rescaling. The proof does not require an attained minimizing road. Blocked use: ['Compare infima over different road classes as if they satisfied the stated contraction.', 'Rescale physical costs along with spatial units.', 'Iterate before fixing the geometry and verifying admissibility.']
- **limit-infinite-lattice-matching** (nonconstructive): The bounded-displacement lattice matching is obtained by a compactness limit on an infinite graph. The proof does not supply a terminating computation of the whole lattice bijection. Blocked use: ['Treat the infinite matching existence theorem as a finite matching algorithm for every lattice site.', 'Claim a finite test certifies the entire infinite bijection.']
- **limit-fixed-direction-event** (formal_scope): Directional geodesic uniqueness and exclusion are asserted for a direction fixed before its probability-one event. The corollary does not supply simultaneous uniqueness for all directions or simultaneous exclusion of all bigeodesics. Blocked use: ['Intersect an uncountable family of directional events without justification.', 'Use the directional corollary alone to exclude every environment-dependent bigeodesic direction.', 'Transfer the exponential single-direction conclusion to all Gamma laws from differentiability alone.']
- **limit-midpoint-distance-and-prefactor** (hypothesis): The quantitative midpoint estimate requires the stated minimum separation from both endpoints. Its constant may depend on Gamma shape; rate uniformity follows from common positive scaling and does not give uniformity over shape. Blocked use: ['Apply the decay estimate when the tested vertex coincides with an endpoint.', 'Assume a single numerical prefactor for every Gamma shape.', 'Interpret the probability bound as an exact finite-geodesic visitation probability.']
- **limit-cone-tip-competition-configuration** (hypothesis): Cone-tip survival concerns the specified simultaneous initial configuration, fixed orientation, closed cone, and a shared Gamma passage metric. Below the threshold it asserts positive survival probability, not survival almost surely. Blocked use: ['Apply the threshold to unequal rates or independent type-specific metrics.', 'Replace the infinite cone seed set by arbitrary finite seed sets.', 'Infer certain survival below the critical half-angle.', 'Treat the orientation-dependent probability assertion as simultaneous pathwise survival across all orientations.']

### Formal statement (Lean 4)

Corpus status: formalized in the source corpus (toolchain `leanprover/lean4:v4.34.1`, Mathlib `d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612`). Not re-checked here; the statements give the exact quantifiers and hypotheses, not a proof.

Scope note of family 212 (`lean/docs/212.md`, verbatim):

> The following describes the scope of the Lean formalization related to the following accompanying paper(s):
>
> - [Strict convexity and differentiability of the planar exponential first-passage limit shape](../../preprints/Strict-convexity-and-differentiability-of-the-planar-exponential-first-passage-limit-shape-September-24-2026/main.pdf)
>
> ## Scope
>
> The formalization proves differentiability of the planar first-passage time-constant norm for independent Gamma edge weights of every positive shape and rate. The norm is differentiable away from the origin, and its unit sphere has a $C^1$ boundary. This includes the exponential model, for which the linked statement also gives a unique supporting line at every boundary point.
>
> The paper also claims strict convexity for the exponential limit shape. Strict convexity is outside these selected differentiability statements.

```lean
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.List.Basic
import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Prod
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Defs
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.LocallyConvex.WithSeminorms
import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Exponential
import Mathlib.Probability.Independence.Basic

namespace OAI

namespace PlanarFPP

open Set MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Filter
open scoped Topology

abbrev Vertex := ℤ × ℤ

abbrev Edge := Vertex × Bool

inductive Step where
  | east | west | north | south
  deriving DecidableEq

def Step.delta : Step → Vertex
  | .east => (1, 0)
  | .west => (-1, 0)
  | .north => (0, 1)
  | .south => (0, -1)

def Step.edge (p : Vertex) : Step → Edge
  | .east => (p, false)
  | .west => (p + (-1, 0), false)
  | .north => (p, true)
  | .south => (p + (0, -1), true)

def displacement (ds : List Step) : Vertex := (ds.map Step.delta).sum

def pathCost (τ : Edge → ℝ) (p : Vertex) : List Step → ℝ
  | [] => 0
  | d :: ds => τ (d.edge p) + pathCost τ (p + d.delta) ds

abbrev Plane := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)

noncomputable def latticeFloor (v : Plane) : Vertex := (⌊v 0⌋, ⌊v 1⌋)

noncomputable def passageTime (τ : Edge → ℝ) (p q : Vertex) : ℝ :=
  sInf {t | ∃ ds : List Step, p + displacement ds = q ∧ pathCost τ p ds = t}

structure TimeConstantNorm (μ : Plane → ℝ) : Prop where
  nonneg : ∀ v, 0 ≤ μ v
  zero_iff : ∀ v, μ v = 0 ↔ v = 0
  triangle : ∀ v w, μ (v + w) ≤ μ v + μ w
  homogeneous : ∀ (a : ℝ) v, μ (a • v) = |a| * μ v

structure ExponentialEnvironment {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (P : Measure Ω) (τ : Edge → Ω → ℝ) : Prop where
  probability : IsProbabilityMeasure P
  measurable : ∀ e, Measurable (τ e)
  independent : iIndepFun τ P
  marginal : ∀ e, Measure.map (τ e) P = expMeasure 1

def IsTimeConstant {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (P : Measure Ω) (τ : Edge → Ω → ℝ) (μ : Plane → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : Plane, ∀ᵐ ω ∂P,
    Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => passageTime (fun e => τ e ω) (0, 0)
      (latticeFloor (t • v)) / t) atTop (𝓝 (μ v))

def DifferentiableAwayFromOrigin (μ : Plane → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : Plane, v ≠ 0 → ∃ ℓ : Plane →L[ℝ] ℝ, HasFDerivAt μ ℓ v

def UniqueNormalizedSupports (μ : Plane → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : Plane, μ v = 1 → ∃! ℓ : Plane →L[ℝ] ℝ,
    ℓ v = 1 ∧ ∀ w, ℓ w ≤ μ w

def C1UnitSphere (μ : Plane → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : Plane, μ v = 1 → ∃ U : Set Plane, IsOpen U ∧ v ∈ U ∧
    ∃ g : Plane → ℝ, ContDiffOn ℝ 1 g U ∧
      (∀ w ∈ U, μ w = 1 ↔ g w = 0) ∧
      ∀ w ∈ U, g w = 0 → ∃ ℓ : Plane →L[ℝ] ℝ,
        HasFDerivAt g ℓ w ∧ ℓ ≠ 0

def HasC1CurveChart (S : Set Plane) (v : Plane) : Prop :=
  ∃ U : Set Plane, IsOpen U ∧ v ∈ U ∧ v ∈ S ∧ ∃ γ : ℝ → Plane, ∃ θ : Plane → ℝ,
    ContDiff ℝ 1 γ ∧ ContinuousOn θ U ∧
    (∀ t, γ t ∈ S ∩ U) ∧ (∀ t, θ (γ t)=t) ∧
    (∀ z ∈ S ∩ U, γ (θ z)=z) ∧
    (∀ t, ∃ d : Plane, HasDerivAt γ d t ∧ d ≠ 0)

theorem manuscriptMain (Ω : Type) [MeasurableSpace Ω] (P : Measure Ω) (τ : Edge → Ω → ℝ)
    (henv : ExponentialEnvironment P τ) :
    ∃ μ : Plane → ℝ, TimeConstantNorm μ ∧ IsTimeConstant P τ μ ∧
      DifferentiableAwayFromOrigin μ ∧ UniqueNormalizedSupports μ ∧ C1UnitSphere μ ∧
      (∀ v ∈ frontier {z | μ z ≤ 1}, ∃! L : Set Plane,
        ∃ g : Plane →L[ℝ] ℝ, g ≠ 0 ∧ (∀ z, μ z ≤ 1 → g z ≤ g v) ∧ L={z | g z=g v}) ∧
      (∀ v ∈ frontier {z | μ z ≤ 1}, HasC1CurveChart (frontier {z | μ z ≤ 1}) v) := by
  sorry

end PlanarFPP

end OAI
```

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


We prove that the limit shape of undirected nearest-neighbor first-passage percolation on ℤ<sup>2</sup> with independent exponential edge weights is strictly convex and has a <i>C</i><sup>1</sup> boundary. This resolves the strict convexity and differentiability conjectures for the planar exponential model. More generally, we prove differentiability of the time-constant norm for every Gamma edge-weight law with positive shape and rate.

<a id="sec:introduction"></a>
##### Introduction

Give each unoriented nearest-neighbor edge $e$ of $\mathbb Z^2$ an independent positive weight $\tau_e$. The cost $\tau(P)$ of a finite path is the sum of its edge weights, counted with traversal multiplicity. Write $\Delta P$ for its terminal vertex minus its initial vertex. Then $$T(x,y)=\inf_{P:x\to y}\tau(P)$$ is its passage time. All lattice paths in this definition are undirected. For the laws considered here, the shape theorem gives a deterministic norm $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^2$, characterized by $$\frac{T(0,\lfloor tv\rfloor)}t\longrightarrow\mu(v)
 \quad\text{almost surely for each fixed }v\in\mathbb R^2.$$ Its unit ball $\mathcal B=\{v:\mu(v)\le1\}$ is the limit shape. We write $|\cdot|$ for the Euclidean norm unless another norm is specified.

<a id="stmt-thm-exponential-shape"></a>
<div id="thm:exponential-shape" class="theorem">

**Theorem 1** (The exponential limit shape). *For independent exponential edge weights of any rate $\lambda>0$, the norm $\mu$ is Fréchet differentiable on $\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\}$, and its unit ball is strictly convex. In particular, $$\mu((1-t)x+ty)<1
 \quad\text{if }x,y\in\partial\mathcal B,\ x\ne y,\ 0<t<1,$$ and $\partial\mathcal B$ is a $C^1$ curve with a unique supporting line at every point.*

</div>

The differentiability argument applies to a larger family. For $\kappa,\lambda>0$, the Gamma law of shape $\kappa$ and rate $\lambda$ has density $$p_{\kappa,\lambda}(t)
 =\frac{\lambda^\kappa}{\Gamma(\kappa)}
   t^{\kappa-1}e^{-\lambda t},\qquad t>0.$$ The exponential law is the case $\kappa=1$.

<a id="stmt-thm-gamma-differentiability"></a>
<div id="thm:gamma-differentiability" class="theorem">

**Theorem 2** (Differentiability for Gamma weights). *For independent Gamma edge weights with any fixed shape $\kappa>0$ and rate $\lambda>0$, the norm $\mu$ is Fréchet differentiable at every nonzero vector, and $\partial\mathcal B$ is a $C^1$ curve.*

</div>

Strict convexity and differentiability exclude different features of a convex boundary: a flat face has more than one point on a supporting line, whereas a corner has more than one supporting line at a point (Figure <a href="#fig:geometry" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:geometry">1</a>). Theorem <a href="#thm:gamma-differentiability" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:gamma-differentiability">2</a> does not assume strict convexity. The proof of strict convexity in Part [part:strict](#part:strict) uses the exponential law and is independent of the differentiability proof.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
###### History and significance

First-passage percolation was introduced by Hammersley and Welsh (Hammersley and Welsh 1965) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[HW1965](#ref-HW1965)]. The asymptotic-shape theory developed through the work of Richardson (Richardson 1973) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[Richardson1973](#ref-Richardson1973)] and Cox and Durrett (Cox and Durrett 1981) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[CD1981](#ref-CD1981)], alongside Kingman’s ergodic theory of subadditive processes (Kingman 1968) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[Kingman1968](#ref-Kingman1968)]. Although the shape theorem gives a convex deterministic body, its fine geometry is much harder to determine; see the survey of Auffinger, Damron, and Hanson (Auffinger, Damron, and Hanson 2017) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[ADH2017](#ref-ADH2017)]. Theorem <a href="#thm:exponential-shape" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:exponential-shape">1</a> resolves positively the strict-convexity and differentiability conjectures for the planar exponential model.

There are important partial results for both questions. Lalley (Lalley 2003) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[Lalley2003](#ref-Lalley2003)] gave sufficient conditions for strict convexity in the standard lattice model, involving asymptotic straightness and mean-zero scaling limits. In Richardson’s site growth model, Durrett and Liggett (Durrett and Liggett 1981) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[DurrettLiggett1981](#ref-DurrettLiggett1981)] established a flat edge for parameters sufficiently close to one and identified its onset with the threshold of a related contact process. For planar edge first-passage percolation with support minimum normalized to one and an atom of mass $p$ there, Marchand (Marchand 2002, Theorem 1.3) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[Marchand2002](#ref-Marchand2002)] determined the exact flat segment on the first-quadrant unit $\ell^1$ boundary when $p>\vec p_c$, where $\vec p_c$ is the oriented-percolation threshold, and a single diagonal contact point when $p=\vec p_c$. For finite-mean laws in this class with $\vec p_c\le p<1$, Auffinger and Damron (Auffinger and Damron 2013, Theorem 2.1) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[AD13](#ref-AD13)] proved differentiability at the endpoints, including the critical contact point. These last two results concern an atom at a positive minimum; exponential edge weights are nonatomic and have essential infimum zero.

The connection between shape geometry and geodesics was developed by Newman and Licea–Newman (Newman 1995; Licea and Newman 1996) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[Newman1995](#ref-Newman1995), [LiceaNewman1996](#ref-LiceaNewman1996)]. Curvature hypotheses and fixed-direction uniqueness play distinct roles in those results. Damron and Hanson (Damron and Hanson 2017) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[DH2017](#ref-DH2017)] proved convergence and coalescence toward a specified supporting sector under differentiability assumptions. Our two regularity conclusions make that sector a single direction. Section 10 states the resulting geodesic and Busemann conclusions with the direction fixed before the probability-one event is chosen. The midpoint question of Benjamini, Kalai, and Schramm (Benjamini, Kalai, and Schramm 2003) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[BKS2003](#ref-BKS2003)] is already answered qualitatively without shape regularity by Ahlberg and Hoffman (Ahlberg and Hoffman 2019) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[AH2019](#ref-AH2019)]. We explain its relation to the directional results. For all Gamma laws, differentiability supplies infinitely many extreme points, making the quantitative midpoint estimate of Dembin, Elboim, and Peled (Dembin, Elboim, and Peled 2024) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[DEP2024](#ref-DEP2024)] applicable as well.

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
###### Proof strategy

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
###### Excluding a corner.

Suppose two distinct extreme supporting functionals $f_-,f_+$ touch the norm in a direction $u$, and let $f=(f_-+f_+)/2$. Their gap gives a linear penalty for transverse motion. Part [part:differentiability](#part:differentiability) turns this penalty into a positive excess over $f$ for every sufficiently long simple path, contradicting the shape theorem along $u$.

First, a crossing confined to a long narrow strip is unlikely to save a fixed multiple of the strip width over either extreme support. Otherwise independent parallel trials, connected using one-sided first-order contact with the norm, would yield macroscopic travel below that support. Second, a finite-region change of measure produces characteristic lengths $L$ for widths $s$, with $L/s\to\infty$ and $L\le s^3$. Nested grids then extend the crossing estimate to arbitrary endpoints, with a summable cost. Third, every cheap path chunk contains a witness for a rare decreasing event. The van den Berg–Kesten inequality (Berg and Kesten 1985) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[BK85](#ref-BK85)], applied to disjoint edge witnesses, handles repeated visits to the same coarse box and yields a bound for all long simple paths at once. The counting builds on Kesten’s rectangle itineraries and crossing-multiplicity estimates (Kesten 1980, sec. 3) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[Kesten1980](#ref-Kesten1980)]; here the local witnesses certify negative excess relative to a supporting functional.

The Gamma extension is built into this proof. Its distributional inputs are exponential tails for short coordinate paths, a continuous quantile representation for the witness inequality, and an exact likelihood calculation: scaling one Gamma weight by $1-\delta$ gives likelihood second moment $(1-\delta^2)^{-\kappa}$. Scaling $O(ns)$ weights with $\delta$ of order $s/n$ has bounded second moment when $n=s^3$. No differentiability or curvature estimate for $\mu$ enters these inputs.

<a id="pm-h-6"></a>
###### Excluding a flat face.

Under a hypothetical flat face, the stationary cocycle construction of Damron and Hanson (Damron and Hanson 2014) <a id="pm-cite-17"></a>[[DH2014](#ref-DH2014)] supplies an additive random function $B(x,y)$, with mean the supporting functional and with $|B(x,y)|\le T(x,y)$. Thus a path from $x$ to $y$ has nonnegative defect $\tau(P)-B(x,y)$. Part [part:strict](#part:strict) considers local random paths, called roads, tracking two directions near the ends of the face. At lattice scale $n$, let $b(n)$ be the infimum of a common upper bound for their mean defect per period. A local perturbation gives $b(n)\ge c_0>0$. The main construction gives a fixed integer $D$ and $\rho<1$ such that $$b(Dn)\le\rho b(n).$$ Iteration contradicts the positive lower bound.

A finite-cell projection constructs local endpoint potentials approximating increments of the generally nonlocal cocycle; interpolation controls every possible attachment in a bounded road interval (Section 3). A physical routing argument bounds the savings obtainable from a selected collection of local shortcuts (Proposition <a href="#access:collection" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="access:collection">47</a>). An area-preserving deformation then controls those savings along paths concentrated near an extreme direction (Lemma <a href="#probability:thin-tails" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="probability:thin-tails">40</a>). Passage-time concentration and mean approximation estimates of Damron–Hanson–Sosoe (Damron, Hanson, and Sosoe 2014) <a id="pm-cite-18"></a>[[DHS2014](#ref-DHS2014)] and Damron–Kubota (Damron and Kubota 2016) <a id="pm-cite-19"></a>[[DK2016](#ref-DK2016)] supply the quantitative metric input.

These estimates let a long geodesic toward an extreme endpoint supply many crossings between neighboring walls while controlling the discarded pieces. The extraction gives a small upper bound for the mean clipped cost of a local crossing. Comparing this crossing with the current road, including the short wall connections, transfers the clipped bound to a primary candidate. To control the remaining large positive costs, a local rule groups their flags into short clusters and traverses an independently built spare road across each accepted cluster, with forward connections at both ends (Lemma <a href="#improvement:replacement" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="improvement:replacement">53</a>). A matched cap controls the frequency of flags, while separation and first-moment estimates control the added cost. This reduces the full expected excess per road period. A fixed rescaling restores the required tracking and locality, so the improved paths belong to the class defining $b(n)$.

The two arguments use different endpoint corrections. In Part [part:differentiability](#part:differentiability), the deterministic defect $\tau(P)-f(\Delta P)$ can be negative. In Part [part:strict](#part:strict), the cocycle defect is nonnegative on every forward subpath. Each part introduces its own local coordinates and parameters.

<a id="model:section"></a>
<a id="part:differentiability"></a>
### Differentiability for Gamma weights

<a id="df:sec:setup"></a>
##### Shape estimates and supporting functionals

Fix $\kappa,\lambda>0$ throughout this part and write $\mu=\mu_{\kappa,\lambda}$. All constants and scale thresholds may depend on this fixed law. We shall compare path costs with the two extreme supporting functionals at a prescribed direction. The crossing estimates use only their one-sided contact with $\mu$; the assumption that they differ enters the final contradiction.

<a id="pm-h-9"></a>
###### Uniform shape and local sums

<a id="df:eq:uniform-shape"></a>
<a id="df:eq:norm-bounds"></a>
We first record the precise form of the standard shape theorem that will be used. It holds for the fixed Gamma law: $$\label{df:eq:uniform-shape}
 \sup_{z\in\mathbb Z^2:\,|z|\ge R}
 \frac{|T(0,z)-\mu(z)|}{|z|}\longrightarrow0
 \qquad\text{almost surely as }R\to\infty.$$ This is the shape theorem of (Krishnan, Rassoul-Agha, and Seppäläinen 2023, Theorem A.1 and Equation (A.3)) <a id="pm-cite-20"></a>[[KRS23](#ref-KRS23)], at weight shift zero. The Gamma law has essential infimum zero and no atom there. For four independent copies of an edge weight, $$\mathbb E\!\left[\min\{\tau_1,\tau_2,\tau_3,\tau_4\}^2\right]
 \le \mathbb E[\tau_1^2]
 =\frac{\kappa(\kappa+1)}{\lambda^2}<\infty.$$ These facts verify the cited hypotheses. The source uses $\ell^1$ distance, which gives <a href="#df:eq:uniform-shape" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="df:eq:uniform-shape">[df:eq:uniform-shape]</a> by equivalence of norms. There are deterministic constants $0<\alpha\le\beta<\infty$ such that $$\label{df:eq:norm-bounds}
 \alpha|z|\le\mu(z)\le\beta|z|\qquad(z\in\mathbb R^2).$$ An event expressed relative to a deterministic lattice origin has the same probability at every translate. This observation will allow us to use shape estimates in probability at origins that vary with the scale. Equation <a href="#df:eq:uniform-shape" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="df:eq:uniform-shape">[df:eq:uniform-shape]</a> itself is an almost-sure statement simultaneously over all endpoints from the fixed origin.

Almost surely every edge weight is finite and positive, since there are only countably many edges. In particular, loop erasure does not increase cost. A path constrained to a set will mean a path all of whose vertices belong to that set; such path-existence events use only its internal edges. Concatenated paths may retrace edges, with each traversal contributing to the cost.

The following bound controls the vertical attachments used below.

<a id="stmt-df-ga-moment"></a>
<div id="df:ga:moment" class="lemma">

**Lemma 3** (Gamma exponential moments). *For $\tau\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(\kappa,\lambda)$ and $\theta<\lambda$, $$\mathbb Ee^{\theta\tau}
 =\left(\frac{\lambda}{\lambda-\theta}\right)^\kappa.$$ If $V$ is the sum over a deterministic set of $M$ distinct edges and $M\le A v$, where $A,v>0$, then <a id="df:eq:gamma-sum-tail"></a>$$\label{df:eq:gamma-sum-tail}
 \mathbb P\left(V>\frac{2A\kappa}{\lambda}v\right)
 \le \exp\{-A\kappa(1-\log 2)v\}.$$*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-df-ga-moment"><summary>Proof of stmt-df-ga-moment</summary>

*Proof.* Integrating the Gamma density with the substitution $y=(\lambda-\theta)t$ gives the moment identity. At $\theta=\lambda/2$ it reads $\mathbb Ee^{\lambda\tau/2}=2^\kappa$. Independence and exponential Markov inequality give $$\mathbb P\left(V>\frac{2A\kappa}{\lambda}v\right)
 \le e^{-A\kappa v}2^{\kappa M}
 \le e^{-A\kappa(1-\log 2)v}.$$ ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-10"></a>
###### The two extreme supports

Signed coordinate permutations preserve the law and hence $\mu$. Together with positive homogeneity, these symmetries reduce the proof to directions $$u=(1,b),\qquad -1\le b\le1.$$ Fix such a deterministic direction for the rest of the argument, and write $$x(z)=z_1,\qquad r(z)=z_2-bz_1,
 \qquad m_0=\mu(u)>0.$$ The function $t\mapsto\mu(u+te_2)$ is convex and Lipschitz. Let $$a_- = \lim_{t\uparrow0}\frac{\mu(u+te_2)-m_0}{t},
 \qquad
 a_+ = \lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{\mu(u+te_2)-m_0}{t}.$$ These finite limits satisfy $a_-\le a_+$. Define <a id="df:eq:support-definitions"></a>$$\label{df:eq:support-definitions}
 \begin{split}
 f_\pm(z)&=m_0x(z)+a_\pm r(z),\\
 a&=\frac{a_-+a_+}{2},\qquad
 c=\frac{a_+-a_-}{2},\qquad
 f(z)=m_0x(z)+ar(z).
 \end{split}$$

<a id="stmt-df-prelim-supports"></a>
<div id="df:prelim:supports" class="lemma">

<a id="df:eq:support-contact"></a>
**Lemma 4** (One-sided contact). *The linear functionals $f_-$, $f_+$, and $f$ are bounded above by $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^2$ and equal $\mu$ at $u$. For $\sigma\in\{-,+\}$, with the corresponding numerical sign when multiplied by a scalar, $$\label{df:eq:support-contact}
 \mu(u+te_2)-f_\sigma(u+te_2)=o(|t|)
 \qquad(t\to0,\ \sigma t>0).$$*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-df-prelim-supports"><summary>Proof of stmt-df-prelim-supports</summary>

*Proof.* Each of $a_-$ and $a_+$ is a subgradient at zero of the convex function $t\mapsto\mu(u+te_2)$. If $x(z)>0$, write $z=x(z)(u+r(z)x(z)^{-1}e_2)$ and use positive homogeneity to get $f_\sigma(z)\le\mu(z)$. If this inequality failed at any other point $z$, then a sufficiently small positive convex combination of $z$ with $u$ would still violate it, by convexity, and would have positive first coordinate. This is impossible. The average $f$ is also bounded above by $\mu$. Equation <a href="#df:eq:support-contact" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="df:eq:support-contact">[df:eq:support-contact]</a> is the respective one-sided derivative expansion. ◻

</details>

<a id="df:eq:minimum-defect"></a>
The *defect* of a path is its cost minus the value of a supporting functional on its displacement. We shall use <a id="df:eq:defects"></a>$$\label{df:eq:defects}
 H(P)=\tau(P)-f(\Delta P),\qquad
 H_\sigma(P)=\tau(P)-f_\sigma(\Delta P).$$ They are additive under concatenation, and $$\label{df:eq:minimum-defect}
 \min\{H_+(P),H_-(P)\}=H(P)-c|r(\Delta P)|.$$ The crossing and endpoint estimates will hold for both signs whether or not $c$ is positive. In Section 5, the gap assumption $c>0$ and <a href="#df:eq:minimum-defect" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="df:eq:minimum-defect">[df:eq:minimum-defect]</a> will make transverse exits expensive relative to the average support $f$.

<a id="df:sec:crossings"></a>
##### Localized crossings

The main estimate in this section is Lemma <a href="#df:cr:rare-fast" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="df:cr:rare-fast">8</a>: a crossing confined to a strip of width of order $s$ is unlikely to have defect below $-\varepsilon s$ when its length is much larger than $s$. The proof amplifies any positive probability of such a crossing into an infinite concatenation whose defect decreases linearly, contradicting the shape theorem.

We prepare three ingredients for this construction. The shape theorem first gives short paths confined near their joining segments. A finite net then makes this assertion simultaneous over all endpoints in two intervals. Finally, an oriented-percolation argument joins sufficiently likely local tests even when nearby tests overlap. Throughout the section, distances are Euclidean unless indicated otherwise. A path constrained to a region has all its vertices there, so its existence and cost are tested using only edges with both endpoints in that region.

<a id="stmt-df-cr-local-travel"></a>
<div id="df:cr:local-travel" class="lemma">

**Lemma 5** (Localized travel). *Fix $D,\eta,\delta>0$. Uniformly over deterministic vertices $p,q\in\mathbb Z^2$ with $|q-p|\le Ds$, the probability tends to one as $s\to\infty$ that there is a path from $p$ to $q$ with cost at most $$\mu(q-p)+\eta s$$ whose vertices are within distance $\delta s$ of the segment $[p,q]$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-df-cr-local-travel"><summary>Proof of stmt-df-cr-local-travel</summary>

<a id="df:eq:cr-uniform-shape"></a>
<a id="df:eq:cr-escape"></a>
*Proof.* *Uniform shape estimates.* Use the constants $\alpha,\beta$ from <a href="#df:eq:norm-bounds" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="df:eq:norm-bounds">[df:eq:norm-bounds]</a>. Equation <a href="#df:eq:uniform-shape" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="df:eq:uniform-shape">[df:eq:uniform-shape]</a> implies, for each fixed $C>0$, $$\label{df:eq:cr-uniform-shape}
 \frac1s\max_{\substack{z\in\mathbb Z^2\\|z|\le Cs}}
       \left\lvert T(0,z)-\mu(z)\right\rvert\longrightarrow0
 \qquad\text{almost surely}.$$ Indeed, outside any sufficiently large fixed ball the error is bounded by an arbitrarily small multiple of $|z|$, while the finitely many passage times inside that ball contribute $o(s)$. The same shape theorem gives $$\label{df:eq:cr-escape}
 \mathbb P\left(
   \inf_{\substack{z\in\mathbb Z^2\\|z|\ge\delta s/3}}
       T(0,z)\ge\alpha\delta s/6
       \right)\longrightarrow1.$$ Translation invariance gives the same probability bounds at every deterministic lattice origin. This uniformity will allow the origins to depend on the endpoints and on $s$.

*Short pieces cannot escape.* Choose a fixed integer $B$ so large that $\beta D/B<\alpha\delta/24$. Round the $B+1$ equally spaced points of $[p,q]$ to vertices $p_0=p,p_1,\ldots,p_B=q$. Uniformly in the endpoints, $$\mu(p_{j+1}-p_j)=\frac{\mu(q-p)}{B}+O(1).$$ Apply <a href="#df:eq:cr-uniform-shape" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="df:eq:cr-uniform-shape">[df:eq:cr-uniform-shape]</a> and <a href="#df:eq:cr-escape" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="df:eq:cr-escape">[df:eq:cr-escape]</a> at these finitely many deterministic vertices. With probability tending to one, uniformly in $p,q$, every short passage time is at most $$\frac{\mu(q-p)}B+
       \min\left\{\frac{\eta}{2B},\frac{\alpha\delta}{24}\right\}s,$$ and escape from the ball of radius $\delta s/3$ about its starting vertex costs at least $\alpha\delta s/6$. For each $j=0,\ldots,B-1$, choose a path from $p_j$ to $p_{j+1}$ with cost at most $T(p_j,p_{j+1})+1$. For all sufficiently large $s$, each chosen path has cost strictly below the corresponding escape bound. Nonnegativity of the weights forces it to stay inside the ball about $p_j$: its initial portion up to a vertex outside would already cost at least the escape bound.

*Concatenation.* Concatenating the $B$ paths gives total cost at most $\mu(q-p)+\eta s/2+B\le\mu(q-p)+\eta s$. Each ball is centered within bounded distance of the original segment, so it lies in its $\delta s$-neighborhood for large $s$. All probability bounds used above are uniform in the deterministic vertices, proving the stated uniformity. ◻

</details>

The next form permits the endpoints to be selected after the environment is observed. The intervals themselves remain deterministic, and the assertion holds for every endpoint pair on one event of high probability.

<a id="stmt-df-cr-interval-travel"></a>
<div id="df:cr:interval-travel" class="lemma">

**Lemma 6** (Travel between intervals). *Fix $D,\eta,\delta>0$. Let $I_1,I_2$ be deterministic vertical intervals on lattice columns, and suppose that the diameter of $I_1\cup I_2$ is at most $Ds$. Uniformly over their locations, with probability tending to one as $s\to\infty$, every pair $p\in I_1\cap\mathbb Z^2$, $q\in I_2\cap\mathbb Z^2$ can be joined by a path of cost at most $\mu(q-p)+\eta s$ within distance $\delta s$ of $[p,q]$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-df-cr-interval-travel"><summary>Proof of stmt-df-cr-interval-travel</summary>

*Proof.* The assertion is vacuous if either interval contains no vertex.

*Finite nets and vertical attachments.* Let $\beta$ be the upper norm bound in <a href="#df:eq:norm-bounds" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="df:eq:norm-bounds">[df:eq:norm-bounds]</a>, and choose a fixed $\gamma>0$ so small that $$\left(\frac{4\kappa}{\lambda}+2\beta\right)\gamma\le\eta/2,
 \qquad \gamma\le\delta/2.$$ In each interval, choose a net of lattice vertices containing its extreme lattice vertices and having consecutive gaps at most $\lfloor\gamma s\rfloor$. For all large $s$, each net needs at most $2D/\gamma+2$ vertices. Assign every interval vertex to a net vertex at vertical distance at most $\gamma s$, using only edges of its intervening gap.

For any such gap, the total weight $V$ is a sum of at most $\lfloor\gamma s\rfloor$ independent edge weights. Lemma <a href="#df:ga:moment" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="df:ga:moment">3</a>, with $A=\gamma$ and $v=s$, gives $$\mathbb P\left(V>\frac{2\kappa}{\lambda}\gamma s\right)
 \le e^{-\kappa(1-\log2)\gamma s}.$$ There are only boundedly many gaps. Thus, with probability tending to one, all vertical connections from interval vertices to their chosen net vertices cost at most $2\kappa\gamma s/\lambda$.

*Connections between net vertices.* Apply Lemma <a href="#df:cr:local-travel" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="df:cr:local-travel">5</a>, with errors $\eta/2$ and $\delta/2$, to every pair of net vertices. Its uniformity and the bounded number of pairs give these connections simultaneously.

*All endpoint pairs on the same event.* On the intersection of these high-probability events, take arbitrary $p\in I_1\cap\mathbb Z^2$ and $q\in I_2\cap\mathbb Z^2$. Concatenate their vertical attachments with the path between the assigned net vertices $\widehat p,\widehat q$. The resulting cost is at most $$\begin{split}
 \mu(\widehat q-\widehat p)+\eta s/2
       +\frac{4\kappa}{\lambda}\gamma s
 &\le \mu(q-p)+\eta s/2
       +\left(\frac{4\kappa}{\lambda}+2\beta\right)\gamma s.
 \end{split}$$ The segments $[p,q]$ and $[\widehat p,\widehat q]$ have Hausdorff distance at most $\gamma s$. The choice of $\gamma$ therefore gives both the cost bound and the required localization, including the vertical attachments. The same event works for every $p,q$, and its probability bound is uniform in the deterministic locations of the intervals. ◻

</details>

We will place local crossing and connection tests on an auxiliary copy of $\mathbb Z^2$. The following elementary lemma needs only a uniform bound on their failure probabilities and independence at sufficiently separated sites.

<a id="stmt-df-cr-oriented-paths"></a>
<div id="df:cr:oriented-paths" class="lemma">

**Lemma 7** (High-density oriented paths). *For every integer $k_0\ge0$ there is $\zeta=\zeta(k_0)>0$ with the following property. Let $(G_v)_{v\in\mathbb Z^2}$ be events such that any finite family indexed by sites at pairwise sup distance greater than $k_0$ is independent. If $\mathbb P(G_v^c)\le\zeta$ for every $v$, then with positive probability there is an infinite path starting at $0$, using steps $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$, all of whose sites satisfy $G_v$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-df-cr-oriented-paths"><summary>Proof of stmt-df-cr-oriented-paths</summary>

*Proof.* *A finite reachable set if there is no infinite path.* Call a site good when $G_v$ occurs. Let $S$ consist of the endpoints of finite oriented paths from $0$ for which every site except possibly the last is good. In particular $0\in S$. If $S$ were infinite, the finitely branching tree of these paths would have an infinite branch; every site on that branch would be good. Hence, on the event of no infinite good path, $S$ is finite.

*A surrounding contour forces bad sites.* For such a finite $S$, orient the boundaries of the unit squares centered at its sites counterclockwise and cancel shared sides. The remaining edges form a balanced directed graph and hence decompose into closed directed trails, with no edge repeated in a trail. Repeated vertices are allowed, so corner contacts cause no difficulty. Every edge has an $S$-square on its left and a complementary square on its right. Winding number is additive under cancellation and decomposition. Its total about $0$ is one, contributed by the square centered at $0$; therefore some trail has nonzero winding.

Let $m$ be the length of this trail. Closedness implies that exactly $m/2$ of its steps are upward or leftward. For these steps, the site on the right is respectively an east or north neighbor of the site on the left. The left-hand site must be bad: if it were good, extending a path that reaches it would put this neighbor in $S$ as well.

*Independent bad sites along a fixed contour.* A site borders at most four edges of the trail, so at least $m/8$ distinct sites are forced to be bad. For any fixed candidate trail these sites are deterministic. Greedy selection in a fixed order gives at least $$\frac{m}{8(2k_0+1)^2}$$ of them at pairwise sup distance greater than $k_0$: each selected site removes at most $(2k_0+1)^2$ candidates. Their tests are independent, so the probability of all the badness conditions forced by this particular trail is at most $\zeta^{m/[8(2k_0+1)^2]}$.

*Summing over contours.* Nonzero winding forces $0$ into the coordinate bounding box of the trail. A length-$m$ trail has coordinate spans at most $m$, so it lies in a square of side $O(m)$ about $0$. Choosing its starting vertex and then its step sequence bounds the number of candidates by $C(m+1)^2 4^m$. Consequently the probability of no infinite good path is at most $$\sum_{m\ge4} C(m+1)^2
       \left(4\zeta^{1/[8(2k_0+1)^2]}\right)^m.$$ This is less than one when $\zeta$ is sufficiently small. The argument uses no stationarity assumption on the tests. ◻

</details>

We now combine these ingredients. The relevant defect is measured against one of the extremal supports $f_\sigma$. Its one-sided contact with $\mu$ allows successive crossings to be connected with defect as small a multiple of $s$ as needed, by drifting consistently to the corresponding side of the direction $u$.

<a id="stmt-df-cr-rare-fast"></a>
<div id="df:cr:rare-fast" class="lemma">

<a id="df:eq:cr-rare-fast"></a>
**Lemma 8** (Rare fast localized crossings). *Fix $A,R,\varepsilon>0$ and $\sigma\in\{-,+\}$. As $s\to\infty$ and $n/s\to\infty$, with $s$ real and $n$ a positive integer, $$\label{df:eq:cr-rare-fast}
 \mathbb P\left(
 \begin{array}{l}
 \text{there is a path $P$ from $x=0$ to $x=n$ with}
       \ H_\sigma(P)<-\varepsilon s,\\
 \text{all of whose vertices satisfy }
       -An\le x\le(1+A)n,\quad |r|\le Rs
 \end{array}\right)\longrightarrow0.$$ The same assertion holds, with the same probability, for every exact lattice translate of the event.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-df-cr-rare-fast"><summary>Proof of stmt-df-cr-rare-fast</summary>

*Proof.* Suppose that the probability in <a href="#df:eq:cr-rare-fast" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="df:eq:cr-rare-fast">[df:eq:cr-rare-fast]</a> is at least $p_0>0$ along a sequence satisfying the stated limits. At each auxiliary site we will try several disjoint translates of this crossing event and require connections to both forward neighbors. Enough trials make a successful crossing likely; the one-sided contact estimate makes the connections likely without spending the whole crossing deficit.

*1. Parameters and site geometry.* The dependence radius must be fixed before we choose how many trials to make. Set $$k_0=\left\lceil4(A+3)+8\right\rceil+1$$ and let $\zeta$ be supplied by Lemma <a href="#df:cr:oriented-paths" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="df:cr:oriented-paths">7</a>. Choose a fixed integer $M$ so large that $(1-p_0)^M<\zeta/2$. For each member of the sequence put $$S_0=100M(R+1)\lceil s\rceil,
 \qquad d=\lceil D_0s\rceil,$$ where the fixed constant $D_0$ will be chosen below, after $M$.

Identify the signs $+$ and $-$ with $1$ and $-1$ when they multiply coordinates. For a test site $v=(v_1,v_2)\in\mathbb Z^2$, write $$i=v_1+v_2,
 \qquad X_i=i(n+d),
 \qquad Y_v=\sigma(i+v_2)S_0.$$ An oriented step sends $i$ to $i+1$ and changes $Y_v$ by $\sigma S_0$ or $2\sigma S_0$. Thus every step advances to the next longitudinal block and moves transversely to the same prescribed side.

*2. Independent crossing trials within a site.* At site $v$, make $M$ trials using exact lattice translates of the event in <a href="#df:eq:cr-rare-fast" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="df:eq:cr-rare-fast">[df:eq:cr-rare-fast]</a>, all with initial column $X_i$, and with their strips disjoint and contained in $|r-Y_v|\le S_0/4$. Here is an explicit choice, which also accounts for lattice phases. Put $$h_j=(2j-M-1)\,3(R+1)\lceil s\rceil,
 \qquad
 t_{v,j}=\left(X_i,
    \left\lfloor bX_i+Y_v+h_j+\tfrac12\right\rfloor\right),
 \quad 1\le j\le M.$$ The translated strip has center $r(t_{v,j})$, within $1/2$ of $Y_v+h_j$. For $s\ge1$, consecutive centers are separated by more than $2Rs$, and every strip of half-width $Rs$ lies inside the designated $S_0/4$ window. Thus the trials use disjoint internal edge sets. Translation leaves both displacement and its supporting functional unchanged, so each trial has probability at least $p_0$, exactly as in the original event. Their probability of all failing is at most $(1-p_0)^M$.

<a id="df:eq:cr-connector-region"></a>
*3. Connection tests for every endpoint pair.* For each of the two forward neighbors $v'$ of $v$, impose an additional test. Every vertex on $$x=X_i+n,\quad |r-Y_v|\le S_0/4$$ must be connectible to every vertex on $$x=X_{i+1},\quad |r-Y_{v'}|\le S_0/4$$ by a path of cost at most $f_\sigma$ of its displacement plus $\varepsilon s/2$, lying in $$\label{df:eq:cr-connector-region}
 X_i+n-s\le x\le X_{i+1}+s,
 \qquad |r-Y_v|\le4S_0.$$ These are existence tests using only the internal edges of this region. Requiring every endpoint pair will permit the successful trials to be chosen later, after the environment has been observed.

*4. Choosing the connector length.* We next choose $D_0$ and verify that both connection tests pass with probability tending to one uniformly in $v$. A connector displacement $z$ satisfies $$x(z)=d,
 \qquad S_0/2\le\sigma r(z)\le5S_0/2\le3S_0.$$ Set $C_0=200M(R+1)$, so that $S_0/s\le C_0$ for $s\ge1$. The one-sided expansion <a href="#df:eq:support-contact" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="df:eq:support-contact">[df:eq:support-contact]</a> supplies $h_0>0$ such that $$0\le\mu(u+h e_2)-f_\sigma(u+h e_2)
       \le\frac{\varepsilon}{12C_0}|h|
 \quad\text{if }0<\sigma h\le h_0.$$ Choose $D_0\ge1$ with $3C_0/D_0\le h_0$. For every possible connector, $h=r(z)/d$ is on the required side and has absolute value at most $h_0$. Homogeneity therefore gives $$\mu(z)-f_\sigma(z)
   \le\frac{\varepsilon}{12C_0}|r(z)|\le\varepsilon s/4.$$ This leaves another $\varepsilon s/4$ for the travel error.

The two endpoint intervals have union diameter at most $Ds$ for a fixed $D$ depending only on $M,R,D_0$. Their joining segments have longitudinal coordinates between the two endpoint columns and satisfy $|r-Y_v|\le9S_0/4$. Since $|b|\le1$, moving Euclidean distance $\delta s$ changes $x$ by at most $\delta s$ and $r$ by at most $\sqrt2\delta s$. Thus a tube with any fixed $0<\delta\le1/2$ fits inside <a href="#df:eq:cr-connector-region" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="df:eq:cr-connector-region">[df:eq:cr-connector-region]</a>. Lemma <a href="#df:cr:interval-travel" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="df:cr:interval-travel">6</a>, with cost error $\varepsilon s/4$, proves the required connection assertions simultaneously for all endpoint pairs. Its probability estimate is uniform in the intervals’ locations, including their lattice phases.

*5. A dependence radius independent of the later choices.* Call $v$ good when at least one of its trials succeeds and both connection tests pass. Its bad probability is at most $(1-p_0)^M+o(1)$, uniformly in $v$. We verify that the initially chosen $k_0$ is a dependence radius. Take a sufficiently large member of the sequence that $n\ge d+s$. The entire test at $v$ is supported on internal edges in $$|x-X_i|\le(A+3)n,
 \qquad |r-Y_v|\le4S_0.$$ To compare two sites, use the integer coordinates $i=v_1+v_2$ and $j=i+v_2$. If their support regions share a vertex, the longitudinal and transverse bounds give, respectively, $$|\Delta i|\le2(A+3),
 \qquad |\Delta j|\le8,$$ where $\Delta$ denotes the difference between the two sites. Since $v_2=j-i$ and $v_1=2i-j$, this implies $$|\Delta v_2|\le2(A+3)+8,
 \qquad |\Delta v_1|\le4(A+3)+8<k_0.$$ Tests at sites at pairwise sup distance greater than $k_0$ therefore use pairwise disjoint edge sets and are jointly independent. In particular, the dependence radius does not increase when $M$ or $D_0$ is chosen. The order of choices was consequently legitimate: $k_0$ and $\zeta$ first, then $M$, then $D_0$, and finally a sufficiently large member of the sequence. For that member the bad probability is at most $\zeta$.

<a id="df:eq:cr-linear-deficit"></a>
*6. Concatenation at one fixed scale.* By Lemma <a href="#df:cr:oriented-paths" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="df:cr:oriented-paths">7</a>, with positive probability there is an infinite oriented path of good sites starting at $0$. Fix this one scale $s,n,d,S_0$ and a configuration with such a path. At each visited site choose a successful trial and join it to the next by a tested connector. Prepend a vertical path from the lattice origin to the initial trial’s starting vertex; its defect $H_\sigma$ is a finite random quantity $C$. If $z_t$ is the endpoint of the trial at the $t$th site, with the initial site numbered $0$, additivity gives a path from $0$ to $z_t$ of defect at most $$\label{df:eq:cr-linear-deficit}
 C-(t+1)\varepsilon s+t\varepsilon s/2.$$ The trials and connectors need not be disjoint: costs are counted with edge multiplicities, so their concatenation still bounds passage time from above.

*7. The shape-theorem contradiction.* At that site, $i=t$ and $0\le v_2\le t$. Hence $$x(z_t)=t(n+d)+n,
 \qquad |r(z_t)|\le2tS_0+S_0/4.$$ Thus $|z_t|\to\infty$ and $|z_t|\le C'(t+1)$ for a deterministic constant $C'$ at this fixed scale. The limit here is $t\to\infty$; the parameters $s,n,d,S_0$ remain fixed. On the probability-one event of the origin shape theorem, its uniform outside-ball estimate applies also to these adaptively chosen endpoints and yields $$T(0,z_t)\ge\mu(z_t)-o(t)\ge f_\sigma(z_t)-o(t),$$ where the supporting inequality is from Lemma <a href="#df:prelim:supports" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="df:prelim:supports">4</a>. This contradicts <a href="#df:eq:cr-linear-deficit" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="df:eq:cr-linear-deficit">[df:eq:cr-linear-deficit]</a>, whose negative part grows at least as $t\varepsilon s/2$. The infinite-path event consequently has probability zero, contradicting its construction. No sequence with crossing probability bounded below by $p_0$ exists, proving the asserted joint limit. Exact lattice-translation invariance proves the last assertion. ◻

</details>

<a id="df:sec:scales"></a>
##### Characteristic lengths
